claim: A6: "Randomization floor e_t(k|H_t) ≥ δ (recommend δ≥0.25)", combined with §16.3's "about 5–6 effective classes per decision point, floor δ≥0.25, override depth d≤2", yielding M = δ^{-d} = 16, E[W²] ≤ 16, and the headline budgets "about 5×10^4 conversations to certify a 0.05 gap".
why_wrong: A floor on *every* selector is infeasible for |K| ≥ 5: 5 × 0.25 = 1.25 > 1, and 6 × 0.25 = 1.5 > 1. δ ≥ 0.25 is only satisfiable with |K| ≤ 4, i.e. three generators plus STOP — one fewer than the minimum the experiment section mandates. With the mandated 5–6 classes the feasible floor is δ ≤ 1/6, so M = δ^{-d} = 36 at d = 2, n_eff ≥ nδ^d = n/36, and the linear-in-M rate gives n ≈ 36·log(2000)/0.0025 ≈ 1.1×10^5 for a 0.05 gap — more than double the advertised cost, and the "roughly what a stratified A/B test costs" comparison (an A/B test over 6 arms needs ~10^4 total for 0.05 at σ≈0.5) becomes an order of magnitude apart. Every quantitative claim in §0.2.3, P5, T20(d) and §16.3 inherits the error. This is not a rounding issue: the design's single selling point is that the budget is purchased and small, and the purchase price as stated is unpayable.
minimal_repair: Restate A6 as a floor on the *support of the evaluated targets only*: e_t(k|H_t) ≥ δ for k ∈ supp(π) for any π ∈ Π, with the residual mass spread over the remaining arms; and make the recommendation δ ≥ 1/(2|K|) with |K| declared. Then recompute M, n_eff and every sample-size figure in §0.2.3, P5, T20(d), §16.3 from the actual |K|, and replace the A/B-test comparison with the honest multiple (≈5–10×, plus the cost of the library).

claim: "The baseline needs no weights. V(e) is an unweighted mean, so a union bound of an LCB on V(π) with a UCB on V(e) certifies strict improvement over the natural/logging policy" — presented as the headline deliverable ("a certified strict improvement over the logging policy").
why_wrong: Two defects, both of which let a null learner produce a certified positive result. (i) V(e) is not a substantive baseline, it is an artifact of the design's own composition. §16 requires the randomization to include a negative-control generator on an inert dimension, a copy-receiver placebo arm, a hard answer-withheld arm, and a graded redaction series. Each such arm sits at probability ≥ δ and drags V(e) down. Adding one more deliberately degraded arm mechanically widens the certified gap V(π) − V(e) with zero learning. The headline number is therefore manufacturable by the analyst, and monotone in the number of placebos. (ii) Nothing anywhere in the document requires comparison against a simple untuned protocol. The obvious competitor — a fixed string ("try again", "that's wrong, fix it") repeated twice, or single-shot no-feedback — is never required to be in K, in Π, or in the reporting table. Since such a policy is a choke-point generator, its value is estimable at the same cost, and if the learned policy does not beat it the entire apparatus is decoration. The document's own §12.15 principle ("off-policy evaluation must justify itself") is applied to the estimator but never to the baseline.
minimal_repair: Split the library into an *evaluated* set and a *diagnostic* set: placebo/redaction/negative-control arms go in a separate randomization stratum that is excluded from V(e). Redefine the certificate target as improvement over a pre-registered *named* baseline generator, and add to §16 a mandatory reporting row with four denominators: (a) single-shot no-feedback, (b) fixed-string retry ×2 to a fixed horizon, (c) the logging mixture V(e), (d) the truncated prophet bound. Require the headline gap to be against (b).

location: §8 T16 ("leakage as design, not mediation"), §2 A12, §16.7
claim: "Λ is a function of (Ã_t, H_t) only (A12), so capping it per generator or including binned Λ as a design coordinate involves no post-treatment conditioning, and contrasts of severity/specificity within a Λ bin are identified by T3." Operational recipe: "bin it; stratify randomization on the bin."
why_wrong: In the primary design the treatment is the selector K_t, and Ã_t is drawn *after* K_t from q_{K_t}. Λ(Ã_t, H_t) is therefore a descendant of the treatment — post-treatment, and specifically a mediator of the k→Y effect, since severity plausibly works partly by conveying information. "Pre-receiver-response" is not "pre-treatment". Consequences: (a) within-Λ-bin contrasts of generators are mediator-stratified, not identified by T3, and are exposed to collider bias through unmeasured message attributes that co-determine Λ and Y; (b) the recipe "stratify randomization on the bin" is operationally impossible, because the bin is not known until after K_t has been drawn and a message sampled; (c) "capping Λ per generator" is rejection sampling on a function of the message, which replaces q_k by a truncated kernel with an unknown normalizer — precisely the case D2's own failure catalogue lists as destroying exact propensity computability, and it silently redefines the estimand away from the pinned library (A5/A8). The section's own concession ("the within-Λ̂-bin contrast is a valid causal contrast for a different coarsening… unsigned") understates this: it is not a different coarsening of the treatment, it is conditioning on a post-treatment variable.
minimal_repair: Do not filter and do not condition. Construct leakage level into the library: define pinned generators q_{k,λ} that are *built* to a target leakage level (by construction of their prompts, verified by the scorer), make (k, λ) jointly the selector, and randomize over it. Then Λ-level is a randomized design coordinate in the literal sense and T3 applies with no conditioning. Report the observed Λ distribution per arm as a fidelity check, not as a stratifier. If Λ-capping by rejection is kept anywhere, label it a redefinition of the generator with an uncomputable density, exclude it from P4, and report it as ITT over the unfiltered generator with a bound on the rejection rate.

claim: T8: "Q_t(H_t, STOP) is a known deterministic functional of H_t when the decision-time signal is recorded" — advertised in §0.2.5 as "the stopping decision is a scalar blip with a known stop-arm value" and in §4 as a nuisance asymmetry with "no medical analogue". Simultaneously A11(d) and §16.6 *require* "two prespecified independent measurement channels, one for stopping and one for scoring".
why_wrong: These cannot both hold. Q_t(H_t, STOP) is known only if the terminal outcome Y is a deterministic function of material already in H_t at decision time — i.e. the scoring channel is read at decision time and is therefore available to the stopping rule. That is exactly the shared-channel configuration P24(ii) identifies as manufacturing Θ(σ√log K̄) of pure-noise apparent gain, and that §16.6 forbids. Conversely, if the stopping channel is genuinely independent of the scoring channel, then the known quantity is the stop-arm value *on the stopping channel*, not Q_t(H_t, STOP) for the scored Y; the stop arm then carries an ordinary unknown causal nuisance and the headline asymmetry evaporates, along with the claim that the endogenous horizon "costs nothing extra". The document never separates the programmatic-Y case (where σ = 0, P24 does not bite, and requirement 6 is vacuous) from the judge-Y case (where T8 is false). Every optimal-stopping result in §4 and §7 rests on whichever reading the reader supplies.
minimal_repair: Split T8 into two statements. T8a: if Y = ψ(artifact) is programmatic and deterministic, Q_t(H_t, STOP) is known, the stopping rule may read ψ, there is no winner's curse, and A11(d)/§16.6 should be deleted as vacuous rather than asserted. T8b: if Y is judge-derived, Q_t(H_t, STOP) is an unknown regression, the stop arm carries a causal nuisance like every other arm, and A11(d) applies together with the P24(ii) inflation term. State which case each reported result is in.

location: §2 A2/A8 (frozen receiver, support), §16.3 ("One primary randomized axis"), §8 T16 ("verify that within a bin, message length no longer predicts Y")
claim: The design is claimed to control everything about the intervention that matters, with A2 pinning the receiver and the only named confound channel being answer leakage; the sole length check offered is an observational within-bin regression.
why_wrong: Two receiver-side confounds are structurally present and nowhere handled by design. (i) *Length.* Severity and specificity generators differ systematically in token count; more input tokens change the receiver's behavior independently of semantics (more context to condition on, higher probability of re-deriving the task). (ii) *Position/recency.* The feedback message is always the most recent content in the receiver's context, so a long severe message pushes the original task specification further from the end of the prompt — a documented degradation channel. Neither is a nuisance to be adjusted: both are *caused by the randomized selector*, so they are mediators, and the only remedy offered ("within a Λ bin, message length no longer predicts Y") is a low-power observational regression that conditions on post-treatment variables (same defect as T16 above) and has no stated power calculation. A positive "severity helps" result is fully explained by "longer prompt, task spec re-anchored closer to the generation point".
minimal_repair: Make length and position design coordinates, not diagnostics. (a) Realize each semantic class at two or three pre-registered token budgets, so class and length are crossed and a length main effect is estimable by design. (b) Fix the rendered prompt geometry across arms: re-render the task specification at a fixed token distance from the generation point in every arm, padding with inert filler verified at Λ = 0. (c) Add a filler-only arm (pure context-length increase, no semantic content) to measure the length main effect directly, and report the class effect net of it.

location: §8 T16, definition of Λ: "a placebo solver (a deliberately weakened receiver given the message alone, with task and prior output withheld)"
claim: This placebo solver, plus a reference-model log-likelihood gain on the ground truth, is an adequate proxy for pre-treatment leakage, with the only stated caveat being that the proxy-to-ideal relation is unsigned.
why_wrong: The proxy is mis-specified in a known direction, and the caveat mislabels the problem. A message like "you inverted the sign in the loop bound" or "you forgot the base case" carries near-zero information to a solver that has not been shown the task or the prior output, and enormous information conditional on them. Leakage in multi-turn feedback is almost entirely *task-conditional*, so a task-blind scorer has essentially no dynamic range over exactly the messages that matter, the bins are degenerate, and the measured Λ is systematically near zero for high-leakage messages. The bias is therefore not "unsigned": Λ̂ understates leakage, and understating it makes the leakage-controlled contrast look larger. Relatedly, A12 and A5 impose no architectural bar on the generators themselves seeing the reference answer or test suite: H_1 = X is "task text × environment seed", ψ must have a reference to score against, and "answer-withheld" appears only as one arm among many rather than as a global constraint on the generator's prompt.
minimal_repair: Redefine Λ as conditional information: the log-likelihood gain of a fixed reference receiver on the reference solution given (H_t, Ã_t) relative to given (H_t, null message) — i.e. condition on the task and prior output and withhold nothing but the message. Validate the scorer's dynamic range on a planted set (messages that literally state the fix must score at the top; pure-affect messages at the bottom). Separately, promote answer-withholding from an arm to an architectural invariant: generators receive a redacted view X⁻ with reference/tests removed, enforced by prompt-hash assertion in §16.1, with the answer-visible condition run only as a deliberate positive control.

claim: "A negative-control generator differing only on a causally inert dimension (politeness markers, greeting, capitalization) must return zero; a non-zero effect indicts confounding, judge bias, or a broken weight." §9 closes: "A run that does not report (a)–(d) is not an experiment."
why_wrong: This control has no valid null in the document's own framework. §2 ("LLMs are paraphrase-sensitive") and §11.1 (whose entire ceiling argument presumes within-history phrasing variation may be causally material) assert that a frozen receiver responds differently to stylistic variants. So a non-zero politeness effect is a *true* effect of the intervention on the pinned receiver, not an indictment of the design, and the control cannot distinguish artifact from real sensitivity. It commits precisely the error §11.2 prohibits ("test nothing, estimate": H_0 is a priori false, so rejection is uninformative and non-rejection is an admission of low power). The remaining battery items are conceded weak by the document itself: P18(a) has no power when weights are degenerate, P18(b) is not exact under an adaptive design, P18(c)'s power against state leakage is OPEN. So no item in (a)–(d) has both a valid null and demonstrated power, which inverts §9's closing sentence.
minimal_repair: Replace (d) with two controls whose truth is known by construction. *Guaranteed null:* an arm that perturbs only text rendered to the user-side channel and provably withheld from the receiver's context, using the T25(d) interface isolation — a software-verifiable zero on Y. *Guaranteed positive:* an arm that appends the reference fix, whose effect must be large; report it as the design's measured ceiling and as the scale against which all other arms are read. Rewrite the §9 closing claim to say what (a)–(d) can and cannot detect, with the power of each stated.

location: §8 P24 requirements ("a horizon-invariance calibration test: score one frozen artifact presented as a 1-turn and as a 5-turn conversation") vs §8 P15(f) ("Show the judge only the final artifact, never the transcript")
claim: The horizon-invariance calibration test (also §16.5) certifies that the judge does not bias the estimated optimal horizon.
why_wrong: Under P15(f) the judge's input is the artifact alone, so presenting the same frozen artifact "as a 1-turn" and "as a 5-turn" conversation feeds the judge byte-identical input: the test passes with probability one and has exactly zero power. The channel that actually produces the P24(iii) threshold shift λ → λ − β is the mediated one P15(f) explicitly does not cut: longer conversations produce *stylistically different artifacts* (longer, more hedged, more commented), and the judge rewards those. The document names this mediated path and then offers a calibration test that cannot see it, while §12.7 lists the horizon-bias result as a headline limitation.
minimal_repair: Replace the test with the one the document already has the machinery for: within strata of identical programmatic content signature, regress the judge score on artifact length and style features, and estimate β directly; then report the induced threshold shift β/λ in cost units as a mandatory number. Additionally require reporting the artifact length distribution by horizon arm, since a length imbalance across arms is sufficient to generate the whole horizon result.

location: §12.10 ("Benchmark contamination … attenuates every blip toward zero — so nulls on contaminated tasks are uninformative. Stratify and report.")
claim: Contamination's only effect on the estimates is attenuation toward zero, hence conservatism.
why_wrong: Attenuation holds for content arms but the sign is reversed for the treatment coordinate this project makes central. On a memorized task the receiver is already correct at turn 1, so (i) the STOP blip is *inflated* — stopping immediately is genuinely optimal there, (ii) the cost-priced value E[Y − λC] of any early-stopping regime rises relative to the logging mixture, which keeps talking and keeps paying c_t, and (iii) the learned horizon is biased short. Since the certificate in T20 is against exactly that talkative logging mixture, contamination inflates the certified gap rather than attenuating it: the headline result is *anti*-conservative under the document's own primary objective. Contamination also distorts the reference distribution G_0 in T13 through the C and N components.
minimal_repair: Amend §12.10 to: contamination attenuates content blips and *inflates* stop-arm advantages and cost-priced gaps. Require the certificate and the prioritized net benefit to be reported primarily within the pre-registered uncontaminated stratum, with the contaminated stratum shown separately, and require a per-task contamination score (e.g. turn-1 pass rate under a no-feedback single shot) as a stratification variable in §16.3, not only as a post hoc report.

location: §9 T27 ("the headline experiment") with §5 P5b's narrow deep benchmark slice
claim: "For ranking competing estimators on the same oracle labels the offset cancels and no variance estimate is needed at all" — offered as the validation procedure for choosing among blip estimators, on the deep slice where n_b ≥ 2 (§16.4 recommends n_b ≥ 8).
why_wrong: Offset cancellation makes the ranking criterion unbiased *for each fixed learner*, but selecting the minimum over L candidate learners on a single noisy criterion computed on a deliberately *narrow* slice reproduces exactly the pathology the document quantifies twice elsewhere: the winner's apparent risk is biased downward by roughly σ_R√(2 log L), and the reported "validated" estimator is chosen by that noise. P11 catches this for branch selection and P24(ii) for stopping; §13(a) even cites Andrews–Kitagawa–McCloskey. It is not applied to T27, which is the headline. The deep slice is by design the smallest sample in the study, so σ_R is largest precisely where the selection happens.
minimal_repair: Split the deep slice into a ranking half and a reporting half, and report the winner's risk on the held-out half; or report the ranking with an AKM/Bonferroni-corrected interval and the number of candidates L. In either case report L and the spread of R̂ across candidates, so readers can judge the selection inflation.

location: §5 P5b / §16.4 (deep benchmark slice, n_b ≥ 8 from the same history) with §2 A1 hygiene and §2 A13 / §9 ("temperature 0 is not determinism")
claim: Resettability supplies "real unbiased conditional-effect labels on the real system" (T27), with A1 interference handled by "caching off" and §16.12's check "verify caching changes latency and not tokens".
why_wrong: The deep slice repeatedly re-sends near-identical prefixes for one task instance, which is the maximal-exposure configuration for provider-side prefix/KV caching and batch-level numeric coupling — the very channels §12.13 lists as A1 threats and §9 concedes exist even at temperature 0. Client-side one cannot verify caching is off, and the proposed check cannot detect it: prefix caching changes kernels and numerics, not the token count, so "tokens unchanged" is consistent with cache-induced dependence across branches. This matters more than for ordinary arms because v̂(h) in T27 is estimated from within-node replicates and will absorb cache-induced dependence as if it were independent Monte-Carlo noise, biasing E[v̂] and hence the debiased risk R̂ by an unknown amount. The document's "real ground truth" is thus the most dependence-exposed quantity in the design.
minimal_repair: Interleave branch expansions across task instances with a cooldown rather than expanding a node's arms back to back, and randomize expansion order (already required for the permutation test, but not applied to the deep slice). Power the P18(c) duplicate-arm check specifically on the deep slice and report the duplicate-arm discrepancy alongside v̂ as a headline diagnostic; if the discrepancy exceeds v̂, declare v̂ (and R̂) unusable. Add a fixed-prompt canary battery replayed each block to detect prefix-cache and numeric drift directly.

location: §7 T13/T14 ("With u representing the preorder and G_0 the mid-rank CDF of u(Z) under a prespecified reference π_0 … Then T8 and T9 apply verbatim with Y replaced by Ỹ")
claim: The rank transform Ỹ = 2G_0(u(Z)) − 1 reduces the prioritized objective to a bounded pseudo-outcome to which the backward induction and sequential DR apply verbatim; the stop arm's value remains known.
why_wrong: "Prespecified reference" pins the *regime* π_0, not the *functional* G_0, which is an unknown feature of π_0's terminal law and must be estimated. With Ĝ_0 plugged in, (i) Ỹ_i are not a fixed function of Z_i and are dependent across units, so the martingale-difference argument underpinning T9 and the exact-unbiasedness claim do not apply verbatim; (ii) T8's "the stop arm's value remains known" requires G_0 known at decision time, not merely π_0 named; (iii) the influence function given for θ accounts for the second arm but the document then asserts verbatim reuse of T8/T9 for Ỹ, which is only true for known G_0. §15.6 flags pathwise differentiability as OPEN when u or the tolerances are estimated but never mentions G_0, which is the nuisance that actually has to be estimated in every run.
minimal_repair: Either estimate G_0 on an independent pre-registered reference sample (a separately logged π_0 run, frozen before outcomes are examined), so Ỹ is a fixed known function on the analysis data and T8/T9 do apply verbatim; or cross-fit Ĝ_0 and carry its contribution as an explicit extra term in the influence function, with the exact-unbiasedness claim downgraded to asymptotic. State which, and add G_0 to the §15.6 OPEN item.

location: §5 "Cross-fitting scheme": "Additional clustering for standard errors by … model-version epoch; randomize arms within time blocks so residual provider drift is balanced rather than confounded" vs §2 A2 ("violation makes the estimand undefined, not noisy") and §12.9
claim: Provider drift is manageable by blocking and clustering.
why_wrong: A2 and §12.9 say a receiver-version change makes the estimand undefined and that no standard error can express uncertainty about "the receiver". If that is true, balancing a version change across arms does not rescue anything: it averages two estimands that the document has declared non-combinable, and clustering by epoch prices only sampling variability, not the definitional break. The two prescriptions are mutually inconsistent, and the blocking recommendation is the one an implementer will follow, silently converting an undefined-estimand event into a slightly wider interval.
minimal_repair: Replace "balance the drift" with a tripwire-and-discard rule: a fixed canary prompt battery replayed at the start of every block, compared by the P18(c) two-sample next-token log-probability test with pre-registered multiplicity control; on detection, the affected blocks are excluded and the run is reported as two separate receiver-conditional analyses. Keep time blocking only for within-epoch nuisances (load, latency), and say explicitly that it is not a remedy for version change.

claim: The certificate is stated at confidence 1 − α with log(2/α) in (b), and the sample-size formula in (d) uses log(|Π|/α); the worked numbers use α = 0.05.
why_wrong: (b) as written is a single-policy bound; using it for a policy chosen from Π requires log(2|Π|/α), and the union with the UCB on V(e) in (c) requires splitting α, so the quoted numbers deliver family-wise ≈0.10 for one policy and no uniform guarantee over Π. Also, (a)'s clipping-bias bound E[W²]/M equals 1 at the recommended M = E[W²] = δ^{-d}, which is uselessly large relative to the 0.05 gap being certified; the reason the certificate still works is that W ≤ δ^{-d} almost surely, so clipping at M = δ^{-d} is vacuous and the bias is exactly zero — which the text never says, leaving the reader with a bias bound twenty times the target effect.
minimal_repair: Write (b) with log(2|Π|/α) and state the α-split used in (c); recompute the worked numbers. In (a), state that M is set to δ^{-d} so that clipping never binds and the bias is identically zero in D1, and confine the clipping discussion to designs where W is unbounded.

location: §1, closing sentence: "adjustment is only available once the treatment has been coarsened, because at the fine level there is no cell to adjust within"
claim: Confounding adjustment requires coarsening the treatment.
why_wrong: This conflates identification with nonparametric cell-based estimation, and contradicts T29, which the document itself corrects to "identified at every a of positive probability, merely not regularly estimable". Adjustment at the fine level is available via a model; what is unavailable is a √n-estimable cell-wise contrast. Left as written it reintroduces the very error §11.2 was revised to remove.
minimal_repair: Rewrite as: "and adjustment is regularly estimable only once the treatment has been coarsened; at the fine level the adjusted contrast is identified but has effective sample size n·e^{−Θ(m)} (T29)."

location: §3 P4 (Rao–Blackwellized marginal weights) vs §10 D2 failure catalogue
claim: "Rule: marginalize over every recorded latent randomization whose density you can compute," presented as a free variance reduction.
why_wrong: The rule inherits, per generator, the entire D2 failure catalogue: discarded chain-of-thought, best-of-n or retries, tool calls inside the generator, speculative decoding, template/tokenizer mismatch, and use of the model distribution where a truncated sampler ran. Any one of these makes q_k wrong, and a wrong q_k converts an *exactly unbiased* selector weight into a biased marginal weight. The trade is therefore not free: it exchanges exact unbiasedness — the document's single strongest claim (T9(i)) — for variance, and the recommended diagnostic P18(a) is conceded to have no power in exactly the degenerate-weight regime where the marginalization is most tempting.
minimal_repair: State P4 as opt-in per generator, conditional on that generator satisfying the D2 conditions (plain autoregressive sampling, sampling-time truncated distribution, fully recorded randomness), with the selector weight as the default and the pre-registered decision rule fixed before outcomes are seen. Require both weights to be reported so the reader can see the discrepancy.

claim: "The endogenous horizon costs nothing extra" — STOP is in the action space, the stop-arm value is known, and no censoring correction is needed inside the harness.
why_wrong: Inside D1 the horizon is not endogenous at all: §12.11 and T28 concede the simulated user never abandons, so R_t is entirely the harness's own randomizer. P23's weight ∏ 1/e_t(CONT|H_t) is then pure design noise and the estimator is a needlessly weighted version of the on-policy rollout that E7 says to run instead. Conversely, all of the motivating structure — P21's "satisfied users stop", informative quit hazards, the identified-set width κ_0(π) — lives in logs, where the D3 row concedes A6 "fails structurally for continuation". So §7's apparatus is unnecessary where it is valid and invalid where it is motivated, while §0.2.5 sells it as a free advantage over medical DTRs.
minimal_repair: Say explicitly that in D1 the stopping coordinate is exogenous by construction and that the learned STOP rule is a *protocol* the system imposes, not a model of when users stop; restrict P23 to its one real use (reusing a single logged harness run across many candidate τ without re-rolling out) and state the break-even against direct rollout; move the P21 material into the D3 extension where it belongs, with the non-identification as its headline.

claim: T20(d) / §0.2(3) / §13(b)12: the finite-sample improvement certificate is a headline deliverable, and "at this corrected rate the machinery costs roughly what a stratified A/B test over the m arms costs" — about 5e4 conversations for a 0.05 gap, 1.2e4 at M=4.
location: §6 T20(d); advertised in §0.2 item 3, §13(b)12, and the one-paragraph verdict
why_wrong: The certificate is numerically vacuous at this project's own measured effect size and compute envelope, and the document never checks it against either. (i) Effect size: the only measured headroom is +4.6 points of final hidden-test pass from *oracle* stopping (docs/audits.md A3), and the experiments workstream's sizing simulation with measured inputs puts the true gap against a competent fixed baseline at +0.015 to +0.030 (docs/design_e3_critic_policy.md §12.2). There is no 0.05 gap to certify, let alone 0.10. At gap = 0.03 the same formula gives n >= M*log(|Pi|/alpha)/gap^2 = 16*7.6/9e-4 ≈ 1.35e5 conversations at M=16, or 3.4e4 at M=4. (ii) Budget: docs/measured_calibration.md states, from measurement, that any design needing substantially more than 10,000–20,000 receiver nodes is unaffordable on this machine, and the whole E3 design (tree + depth-2 supplement + a 9-arm live head-to-head) totals ~24,000 calls. The certificate is 20–400x over budget. (iii) Worse, the bound's own half-width at any affordable n cannot resolve the effect: with the pre-registered inference unit being the 176 task families (design §3, §12.3), sqrt(2*M*log(2/alpha)/n_eff) at M=4, n_eff=176 is ≈0.29, and even treating all 1,520 paired units as i.i.d. gives ≈0.14 — 3x to 6x the entire 0.046 of headroom that exists. A one-sided LCB that is always negative certifies nothing.
minimal_repair: Demote T20 from a deliverable to a scope statement: "a finite-sample certificate is available in principle and is uninformative at any n affordable here; we report a family-clustered paired bootstrap CI instead." If a certificate is kept, state the required n as a function of the gap and print the three numbers side by side (required n, affordable n, available gap). Also fix the inference unit: n in the Bernstein bound must be the number of independent clusters (families), not conversations.

claim: A6: "Randomization floor e_t(k|H_t) >= delta (recommend delta >= 0.25)", combined with §16.3's "about 5–6 effective classes per decision point, floor delta >= 0.25"; all estimability arithmetic then uses M = delta^{-d} = 16 (d=2) or 1/delta = 4 (single turn).
location: §2 A6; §16 item 3; P5 bounded case; T20(d)
why_wrong: A floor of 0.25 on every selector requires |K| <= 4 including STOP, since sum_k e_t(k) = 1. §16.3 asks for 5–6 classes plus STOP (6–7 selectors), and the frozen taxonomy actually has 9 actions (design §2, A0..A8; the branch tree uses e = 1/8 over non-STOP arms). The recommended floor is therefore arithmetically impossible for the pre-registered action space, and every downstream number is wrong in the expensive direction: with m = 9, uniform gives delta = 0.111, so M = delta^{-d} = 81 at d = 2 (not 16) and 9 at d = 1 (not 4). T20's linear-in-M rate then multiplies every sample-size figure by 5x (d=2) or 2.25x (d=1) on top of finding 1, and P5's reassuring "delta=0.25, d=2 => E[W^2] <= 16" becomes E[W^2] <= 81. COORDINATION.md Q7 flags exactly this trade ("this sets the number of prompt classes we can afford per decision point") and the theory document answers it with two mutually inconsistent numbers.
minimal_repair: State the constraint explicitly as m*delta <= 1 and pick one side: either delta = 1/m with m = 9 (and re-derive M = 81, n, and the certificate figures), or a floor only on a pre-registered *contrast set* of <= 4 arms with the remainder of the mass unconstrained (and then d, M and Pi must be defined relative to that set). Recompute P5's worked examples and T20(d) with the chosen m.

claim: T8: "Q_t(H_t, STOP) is a known deterministic functional of H_t when the decision-time signal is recorded", hence §0.2(5) "the endogenous horizon costs nothing extra" and §0.3's claim that the only causal nuisance is the continuation value.
why_wrong: This equivocates between two information sets. Y(STOP at t) = psi(artifact in hand) is known to the *analyst* because psi is computed by running hidden tests; it is not a function of the policy's information set. Pi_cp is restricted to choke-point-measurable policies and P23 requires tau to be adapted to decision-time observables, so every implementable stopping rule must estimate E[psi(H_t) | phi(H_t)] — i.e. predict hidden-test pass from the visible conversation, with no hidden tests. The project's own design names this as the single load-bearing model (design §6.4: p_hat_k(s) = P(V=1|S) is "the deployable policy's whole handle on 'am I already right'"), and the evidence that it is hard is already in hand: the visible verdict is one bit on 163/190 tasks and absent on 20.8% of the informative pool (design §3), and the sibling loop's own self-check stopped on 50% of all failures (audits.md A3). The +4.6 point headroom that the whole flagship claim rests on is the value of the *oracle* V, not of any implementable rule. So the endogenous horizon does not cost nothing; it costs the hardest estimation problem in the project, and T8 as written hides it by calling it "a pure prediction problem with no causal content" and then never bounding the value loss it induces.
minimal_repair: Split the history: H_t^A (analyst) and H_t^O = phi(H_t) (policy-observable). Restate T8 as: Q_t(H_t^A, STOP) is known, so the STOP arm carries no causal nuisance and needs no positivity; but sup over Pi_cp of V is bounded by the calibration of E[psi | H_t^O], and add the resulting bound (e.g. achievable gain <= E|P(V=1|H^O) - 1{V=1}| scaled by the repair/breakage rates). Report the oracle-V minus p_hat gap as the headline, as the E3 design already does.

claim: T19 plus §0.3: "a learned blip estimator is mandatory", with the value-loss guarantee V(pi*) - V(pi_hat) <= E|gamma_hat - gamma| (binary one-step) and <= sum_t E^{pi*}[Delta_t] in general, the history-shift factor being "bounded here by design".
why_wrong: The bound is correct and numerically vacuous at every achievable critic precision, so it provides no guarantee for the object the paper is built around. Label noise on the blip pseudo-outcome is Bernoulli: the design's own statement is that at 3 seeds the per-state Monte Carlo SE of gamma is "up to 0.29" (design §8), and the pooled per-row noise SD of a paired binary contrast is ~0.5. With 400 branch states x 8 classes x 3 seeds (~9.6k rows, 87 features) an honest E|gamma_hat - gamma| is O(0.1), i.e. 2–4x the entire 0.046 of available headroom and larger than the true blips themselves (repair 0.239, breakage 0.162 imply |gamma| mostly < 0.25 and often < 0.05). A guarantee of the form "you lose at most 0.1–0.2 of value" on a scale where the total prize is 0.046 is not a guarantee. The document also never states which side of T19 is being claimed for the project's third deliverable — a *generative* prompt policy (README; design §9.2/§9.3) — whose messages leave the pinned library, so by the document's own T26(b) and §12.2 its value is neither identified nor certified and T19 does not apply to it at all. §0.2(4) ("every treatment is a shippable mechanism") papers over that gap.
minimal_repair: Replace the L1 bound with a margin/decision-theoretic statement that can be non-vacuous here (value loss <= E[|gamma| 1{|gamma_hat - gamma| >= |gamma|}]), report the measured distribution of |gamma| and of the critic's per-state error so the reader can see whether the bound bites, and add one sentence to §0.3/§12 saying explicitly that a trained free-form generator is outside every guarantee in the document.

claim: §0.1/§0.2 make design-based *off-policy* identification the primary strategy, and the technical apparatus (T3, P5, P6, P10, T20, estimator menu E1–E6) is built on unpaired i.i.d. units carrying importance weights.
why_wrong: The only affordable experiment is a *paired, common-random-number, on-policy* head-to-head: every arm branches from the same saved root output O_1 per (task, seed), and the design states that without this pairing power at delta = 0.05 is 0.31 while with it it is >= 0.95 (design §11.1). The dominant variance component here is between-task difficulty (Beta(0.348, 0.230), U-shaped), and pairing removes it; no formula in the theory document contains that term. P10's variance decomposition, T20's certificate and the Renyi budget all price a design that nobody will run, while the estimator actually pre-registered (mean over 176 families of family-mean paired differences with a paired cluster bootstrap, design §12.3) does not appear in the menu. The document's own E7/§12.15 ("where the environment is resettable, off-policy evaluation must justify itself") is the correct verdict and it contradicts §0.1's ordering.
minimal_repair: Add a paired/CRN estimator as E0 in the menu with its variance written in terms of Var(D_i) and a paired empirical-Bernstein version of T20 on D_i in [-1,1]; restate §0.1 as "on-policy paired rollout is primary; the off-policy apparatus governs tree reuse across candidate policies and the observational extensions".

claim: §1's confounding narrative — "a bad output provokes a severe correction, so the artifact term is negative and a naive regression reward model learns the wrong sign" — used in §0 and §13(c) to motivate the causal critic.
why_wrong: The project's own premise checks already separated this claim into four pieces and refuted the decision-level one: a correlational, state-conditioned critic recovered the exact optimal regime in 39/40 replicates (regret 0.0010), and under a latent confounder and a swept coupling the logged-minus-randomized regret gap never exceeded 0.030, with known-propensity IPW repairing it only partly and non-monotonically (docs/premise_findings.md C1–C3). The dominant decision-level error was myopia, not confounding. The experiments workstream has pre-registered S1 (causal critic vs matched correlational critic) with "expected value: null" (design §12.3). The theory document's only concession is a parenthesis that the sign is "an empirical conjecture", which understates the position: the reported-effects claim survives, the decisions claim is already evidence-against.
minimal_repair: Rewrite §1's last paragraph to state the split explicitly (adjustment changes *reported* effects by a large margin and *decisions* by a small one, with the P1–P3 numbers cited), and move the motivation of the critic onto horizon-aware valuation and known-propensity design, which is what the evidence supports.

claim: §0.2(5) and A4/A6: STOP is "one of the selectors", sitting in the same finite action space and subject to the same randomization floor delta >= 0.25.
why_wrong: Randomizing STOP at a floor is strictly wasteful and the document's own T8 says why: the STOP arm's potential outcome is analytically known and has zero Monte Carlo variance, so every call spent on a STOP draw buys no information. At delta = 0.25 per turn, a quarter of all decision points are force-terminated, trajectories are depleted geometrically ((0.75)^{t-1}), and late-turn blips — the ones P10 tells you to spend the branching budget on — lose ~44% of their sample by turn 3. The actual design avoids this entirely: the tree randomizes only over the 8 non-STOP classes with e = 1/8 and gets "positivity for A0 is free" from the degeneracy Y(A0) = V_k (design §2). The theory document never notices that its own T8 makes A6's floor on STOP unnecessary and costly.
minimal_repair: Exempt from A6 any arm whose potential outcome is H_t^A-measurable: state the floor over the non-degenerate selectors only, note that STOP positivity holds by degeneracy rather than by randomization, and recompute d, M and the budget with STOP excluded from the randomized set.

claim: T8's non-regularity aside — "report the mass of histories with |gamma_hat| near zero, since that mass drives the non-regularity" — treated as a reporting footnote, and §12 lists no limitation about null-blip mass.
why_wrong: On this task family the exceptional set is not a corner, it is most of the sample space, and the contestable set is a few percent. Audit A2's beta-binomial fit for the 3B receiver puts 0.156 of task mass at hidden-test success < 0.05 (blip exactly 0 for every class: nothing repairs them) and 0.334 above 0.95 (where the blip is dominated by breakage, and the trivial rule "stop iff visible_pass" already captures it, which is why baseline B4 is so hard to beat). The states where a learned critic can beat that trivial rule are essentially the false-pass states, whose rate phi = P(visible pass | hidden fail) is *unmeasured* and assumed to be 0.10–0.25 — which is precisely why the design's power swings from 0.35 to 0.91 across that assumption (design §12.2). So (i) inference on V(pi*) is non-regular over a large fraction of the population, not a measure-zero set, and (ii) any marginal blip is attenuated by the null mass, which is also what §12.10 says about contamination but never says about difficulty.
minimal_repair: Add to §12 a limitation stating the measured null-blip mass and that the primary estimand must be defined conditional on the first attempt failing (as audits.md A2 recommends), with the already-correct stratum analysed separately for harm; and make the non-regularity remedy (m-out-of-n bootstrap or adaptive intervals) a requirement in §16, not a suggestion.

claim: T27 is "the headline experiment": a debiased validation risk giving real unbiased conditional-effect labels on the real system, with the caveat that gamma_tilde is the blip under the branch continuation regime.
why_wrong: The caveat is violated by the only tree that fits the budget, and the offset swamps the signal. (i) The E2 tree branches at depth 1 with *policy-fixed* depth-2 continuations (design §6.3), while the critic's target is the blip under an optimal continuation (max over A_adm inside V_tilde_2). T27 is therefore unbiased for the wrong target by construction, exactly as its own caveat warns, and the depth-2 supplement (200 states x 8 x 2 = 3,200 rollouts) is too small to repair it. (ii) At the affordable 3 seeds per branch, v(h) ≈ p(1-p)/3 ≈ 0.08 (design §8 states SE up to 0.29 per state), whereas the risk being measured, E[(gamma_hat - gamma)^2], is 0.01–0.04 for any plausible critic: the subtracted offset is 2–8x the estimand, and R_hat's Monte Carlo error over ~400 states is of the same order as the difference between a good and a useless critic. (iii) §16 item 4 demands a narrow-deep slice with n_b >= 8, which at 400 states x 8 classes is 25,600 nodes — above the measured 10k–20k node affordability ceiling (measured_calibration.md); at the ~50 states that are affordable, R_hat's error is ~±0.05 and ranks nothing.
minimal_repair: Restate T27 as a *ranking* device only (offset cancels; report the paired difference of squared errors with its bootstrap interval), state the continuation mismatch as a scope restriction on the claim ("validated against the fixed-continuation blip") rather than a caveat, and replace §16's n_b >= 8 demand with the n_b that the node ceiling actually permits together with the resulting resolution.

claim: P4 / §13(b)6: Rao–Blackwellized marginal weights are a technical contribution, with the rule "marginalize over every recorded latent randomization whose density you can compute", and §0.4 lists this as D2's correct role.
why_wrong: In the design that is actually frozen the generators are deterministic template renders with a uniformly drawn template index (design §0.3, §5), so q_k(a|h) is a point mass and distinct k produce distinct texts: the numerator and denominator each collapse to one term, the marginal weight equals the selector ratio exactly, and the variance reduction is identically zero. Where generators are LM-based, computing q_k for the m-1 arms that were not taken requires m teacher-forced scoring passes per turn on the realized message, plus the sampling-time truncated distribution rather than the model distribution — a per-turn cost the document never prices and which competes directly against the branch budget. So the contribution is vacuous in the primary design and non-free in the only design where it bites.
minimal_repair: Add the applicability condition to P4 (non-degenerate, overlapping generator supports and computable truncated densities), state the m-scoring-passes cost per turn, and note that for deterministic template libraries P4 is an identity with no gain.

claim: T20(b)(d): with probability >= 1-alpha the displayed empirical-Bernstein LCB holds, and n ≳ M log(|Pi|/alpha)/gap^2 suffices, with the union of an LCB on V(pi) and a UCB on V(e) certifying strict improvement.
why_wrong: The quoted sample-size constant is optimistic by a factor of roughly 2–8 even on its own terms. Requiring sqrt(2 sigma^2 log(2/alpha)/n) <= gap with the stated variance proxy E[min(W,M)^2] <= M gives n >= 2M log(2/alpha)/gap^2, and the union over |Pi| plus the second (baseline UCB) deviation term in (c) replaces log(2/alpha) by log(4|Pi|/alpha) and splits the gap, costing another factor ~4. The displayed figures (5e4, 1.2e4) drop both. |Pi| = 100 is also not the right complexity term once pi_hat is an argmax over a boosted critic; with cross-fitting the certificate must be evaluated out-of-fold and the effective n divides by the number of folds.
minimal_repair: Write the constant out (n >= 8M log(4|Pi|/alpha)/gap^2 for a two-sided union at gap/2 per side), state that |Pi| must be a pre-registered finite class or replaced by a fold-wise certificate with n/K per fold, and re-quote the worked numbers.

claim: P24(ii): if the stopping rule is chosen to maximize the estimated value, the apparent gain is Theta(sigma sqrt(log K_bar)) even when true quality is flat, and "at realistic judge noise and K_bar ≈ 5 this is comparable to any real effect this project hopes to report".
why_wrong: sigma is never defined, and the two readings differ by sqrt(n). If sigma is per-unit outcome noise (~0.43 for a binary verdict) the claimed inflation is ~0.5, which is absurd — it exceeds the outcome range's usable span. If sigma is the standard error of the estimated per-turn value, then at n = 1.5e3–1e4 units sigma ≈ 0.004–0.011 and the inflation is 0.005–0.013, i.e. real but well below the 0.027 MDE and removable by the selection/evaluation split the document already recommends elsewhere (P11). As written, the threat is overstated by about two orders of magnitude, which misallocates the design's attention (and the "two independent channels" requirement is justified by the *differential* bias argument in P15(a), not by this one).
minimal_repair: Define sigma as the standard error of the value estimate at the analysis n, give the resulting numeric inflation, and justify the independent-channel requirement from P15(a) plus P24(iii) instead.

claim: T13/T14: coarsening (Y, C, N) lexicographically and rank-transforming to Y_tilde = 2G_0(u(Z)) - 1 is a contribution that lets correctness-then-cost-then-turns run through the same backward induction, "scale-free ... no hand-tuned lambda".
why_wrong: On this project's outcome the construction is nearly degenerate. Y is a binary hidden-test verdict, N in {1,2,3}, and cost is a monotone function of N up to token noise, so with tolerances eta the ordered quotient has ~6 cells and the tie mass is the majority of pairs (two failures at the same turn count tie exactly). The win-probability estimand is then a coarse monotone re-expression of a 2x3 table, its variance is dominated by tie handling, and it *shrinks* the already marginal effect (0.015–0.030) rather than stabilising it. The pre-registered plan in fact uses a scalar primary with a cost-adjusted secondary at lambda = 0.01/turn (COORDINATION Q5; design §9.1, §12.3), i.e. exactly the priced-cost route T13 claims to improve on.
minimal_repair: Scope T13 to outcomes with a continuous or many-valued primary component; for a binary primary outcome state that the prioritized form reduces to the (Y, N) table and report the tie mass, and keep the priced scalar as primary.

claim: A1 ("Task-level units, no cross-trajectory interference") is marked BC — holds by construction with hygiene — in §2 and in every column of the §10 ladder.
why_wrong: On the machine this will run on, A1 cannot be by construction. The receiver is llama-server with -np 4 under a *foreign* GPU load from two sibling projects' resident servers, the design records yielded_seconds_before_start and foreign_gpu_load_at_start precisely because that load is uncontrolled, and llama.cpp is "not bit-deterministic across batches even at a fixed seed" (design §11.3, §11.4; measured_calibration.md deliberately measures under contention). Batch composition and a shared, drifting external load are common shocks across in-flight units; randomizing batch composition makes the interference exchangeable but does not make it absent, and the theory document's own §12.13 lists these as live channels while §2 still grades A1 as BC.
minimal_repair: Grade A1 as "assumed, with randomized batch composition and a pre-registered drift diagnostic (arm x time-block interaction, foreign-load covariate)" in both §2 and the ladder, and require the diagnostic in §16 item 12.

claim: A6 recommends a randomization floor δ ≥ 0.25 ("BC (δ≥0.25)" in the §10 ladder), and §16 item 3 simultaneously prescribes "about 5–6 effective classes per decision point, floor δ≥0.25". P5 then derives E[W²] ≤ δ^{-d} = 16 at δ=0.25, d=2, and T20(d) prices the whole certificate at M=16.
location: §2 A6; §16 item 3; §4 P5 "bounded case"; §6 T20(d); §10 ladder row A6
why_wrong: Arithmetically impossible. A floor δ on every arm of a finite selector set requires Σ_k e_t(k|H_t) ≥ mδ, so δ ≤ 1/m. With 5–6 classes plus STOP (m = 6–7) the largest feasible floor is 1/6 ≈ 0.167, not 0.25; δ=0.25 admits at most four selectors including STOP. This is not a rounding issue: every headline number in the document is computed from δ=0.25. At the feasible uniform floor δ=1/6 and d=2, M = δ^{-d} = 36, not 16 — a 2.25× inflation of the variance bound and of every sample size derived from it, before any other correction.
minimal_repair: Replace the free-standing "δ ≥ 0.25" with "δ = c/m for a pre-registered c ≤ 1", state the feasibility constraint δ ≤ 1/|K| in A6, and recompute P5's worked numbers and all of T20(d) at the floor the frozen taxonomy actually permits. If δ=0.25 is to be kept, cap the action space at four selectors including STOP and say so in §16.

claim: T20(d): "Sample complexity is LINEAR in M: n ≳ M log(|Π|/α)/gap². Concretely with δ=0.25, d≤2 (M=16), |Π|=100, α=0.05: about 5×10⁴ conversations to certify a 0.05 gap, 1.2×10⁴ for 0.10... At this corrected rate the machinery costs roughly what a stratified A/B test over the m arms costs."
location: §6 T20(d), and the "honest comparison" sentence at the end of it
why_wrong: The quoted numbers drop a factor of ≈8 relative to the document's own display in T20(b). (i) The Bernstein term is sqrt(2σ̂²L/n), not sqrt(σ̂²L/n) — factor 2 inside. (ii) T20(c) certifies improvement by unioning an LCB on V(π) with a UCB on V(e), so each side may spend at most gap/2 — factor 4. (iii) L = log(2|Π|/α) = log 4000 = 8.29 must include the union bound. Correctly: n ≥ 8·M·L/gap² = 8·16·8.29/0.0025 ≈ 4.2×10⁵ conversations for a 0.05 gap, and ≈9.6×10⁵ at the feasible floor δ=1/6 (M=36). The comparison claim then fails outright: a single prespecified two-arm comparison at gap 0.05 on a bounded outcome needs ≈1.3×10³ per arm, and a stratified design over m=6 arms ≈8×10³ — so the certificate machinery costs 50–120× a stratified A/B test, not "roughly" the same. It is also unaffordable on the measured hardware: at ~4 receiver calls per conversation and the project's own measured 2,150 calls/hour (docs/measured_calibration.md), 4.2×10⁵ conversations is ≈790 GPU-hours (≈1,780 h at δ=1/6), against the document-adjacent affordability ceiling of 10,000–20,000 nodes ≈ 9–18 h.
minimal_repair: Recompute (d) as n ≥ 8·M·log(2|Π|/α)/gap², print the corrected figures, delete the "roughly what a stratified A/B test costs" sentence, and state explicitly that the certificate is only affordable for M ≤ 2–4 (single-turn, binary coordinate) at a gap of 0.10 or larger. Report the A/B cost side by side rather than asserting parity.

claim: The certificate and all estimability arithmetic are stated in conversations: "about 5×10⁴ conversations", n=10⁴ in the §4 budget arithmetic — while §1 declares "Task instances i=1,…,n with X_i ~ P_X i.i.d. The unit is the task instance (task text × environment seed)", and §5 requires cross-fitting to put "all branches, replicate seeds, turns and paraphrase variants of one task in the same fold".
location: §1 Units; §5 Cross-fitting scheme; §4 budget arithmetic; §6 T20(d)
why_wrong: The two cannot both hold. Empirical Bernstein (T20b) is an i.i.d. bound over the n summands; §5 concedes that replicate seeds of one task are dependent enough to require common-fold treatment. The project's own audit (docs/audits.md A2) finds the informative pool is ~230 tasks with the 3B receiver (~100 with the 7B), not 590, and per-task effects are strongly heterogeneous and bimodal. Defining the unit as (task text × seed) manufactures unlimited "units" out of a 230-element task population — this is the loophole that makes the sample-size arithmetic look feasible while voiding the independence the bound needs, since the task text is the dominant variance component. At the honest cluster level the certificate is vacuous: sqrt(2·16·8.29/230) ≈ 1.07, larger than the entire range of Y−λC ∈ [0,1]. The flagship guarantee therefore cannot be produced on this task pool at any budget.
minimal_repair: Redefine the i.i.d. unit as the task instance (task text only), state n_clusters explicitly wherever n appears, and replace T20 with a cluster-level certificate (average within task, then bound over ~230 bounded cluster means). Then state plainly that at 230 clusters a 0.05 gap is not certifiable by this route, and make the primary analysis a paired, task-stratified randomized comparison with cluster-robust inference — which cancels the between-task variance and is affordable — rather than an unpaired IPW bound, which cannot exploit pairing.

claim: T8 and §0.2 item 5: "Q_t(H_t,STOP) is a known deterministic functional of H_t", giving "V*_t(H_t) = max{Q_t(H_t,STOP), max_{k≠STOP} Q_t(H_t,k)}, with the optimal regime read off the argmax", advertised as a structural advantage with "no medical analogue" and echoed in the one-paragraph verdict.
why_wrong: The stop-arm value is known only to the *harness*, because knowing it means having graded the current artifact against the hidden tests. The design forbids that grade from reaching the decision (A1's visible/hidden assertion split; A12's leakage control; P23's own requirement that a regime be "adapted to decision-time observables", with "a rule reading an end-of-episode oracle... not a policy but the prophet benchmark"). A regime whose argmax is taken against the harness-known Q_t(·,STOP) is therefore P23's prophet, not an element of Π_cp. The project's own audit says this in units: oracle stopping is worth +4.6 pp but "oracle stopping is not available to any real rule" (docs/audits.md A3). So the advertised advantage collapses to the parenthetical the document buries — "otherwise a pure prediction problem with no causal content" — i.e. predicting the hidden grade from the decision-time signal, which is exactly the self-check classifier the sibling run already ran (and which stopped on 50.4% of failures).
minimal_repair: Restate T8 with Π_cp defined as regimes measurable w.r.t. the recorded decision-time signal φ(H_t), and replace Q_t(h,STOP) with its φ-measurable prediction. Delete "known" from §0.2 item 5 and the verdict, and reframe the stop arm honestly: the causal content is in the continuation value, the stop arm is a supervised calibration problem, and the baseline to beat is the existing self-check rule.

claim: §0.1/§0.2/§13/verdict advertise identification of "the optimal regime" π* = argmax over choke-point-measurable policies with W ≤ δ^{-d}, while §16 item 3 caps "override depth d ≤ 2" and P5 prices everything at d=2.
location: §0.2 item 3 and item 6; §4 P5; §6 T19; §16 item 3; §10 ladder row D1; verdict
why_wrong: Override depth is defined as the number of turns at which π differs from e. Any interesting optimal regime — and certainly the one T19 propagates over T turns under "the optimal regime's history law" — deviates at essentially every turn, so d = T, not 2, and M = δ^{-T}: 1,024 at δ=0.25/T=5, and 7,776 at the feasible δ=1/6. Capping d ≤ 2 restricts the certified policy class to depth-2 deviations from the harness's randomizer, which is not "the optimal regime over Π_cp". The document never reconciles the two, and every sample size, weight bound and certificate is quoted at the small-d figure while the claimed deliverable requires the large-d one.
minimal_repair: Pick one. Either (a) state the deliverable as "certified improvement within the depth-≤2 deviation class" everywhere, including §0 and the verdict, and drop "the optimal regime"; or (b) keep full-horizon π* and quote M = δ^{-T} with the resulting sample sizes, at which point the certificate is dead and the honest route is on-policy rollout of the learned regime (E7).

claim: P5b: "Var(β̂) ∝ (σ_e²/n_b + σ_m²)/n, which (given σ_m²>0) is increasing in n_b once the budget is substituted: for fitting a blip model the budget-optimal design is the widest one (n_b=1 paired contrast per history)" — operationalized in §16 item 4 as a wide-shallow training slice at n_b=1.
why_wrong: False in general. Substituting n = B/(c_0+n_b) gives f(n_b) = (σ_e²/n_b + σ_m²)(c_0 + n_b), whose derivative is σ_m² − σ_e²c_0/n_b². This is negative at n_b=1 whenever σ_e²c_0 > σ_m², so the function is decreasing, not increasing, and the interior optimum is n_b* = σ_e√c_0/σ_m. With this project's plausible values (binary-outcome contrast noise σ_e ≈ 0.5–0.7, roll-in cost c_0 ≈ 2–3 calls, model-misspecification sd σ_m ≈ 0.1) n_b* ≈ 10 — deep, not wide, the opposite of the prescription. The stated conclusion holds only in the regime σ_m² ≥ σ_e²c_0, which is not asserted and is unlikely here.
minimal_repair: State the optimum n_b* = σ_e√c_0/σ_m, note that wide-shallow is optimal only when σ_m² ≥ σ_e²c_0, and make §16 item 4 pick n_b from a pilot estimate of (σ_e, σ_m, c_0) instead of hard-coding n_b=1.

claim: T16: Λ is "a function of (Ã_t,H_t) only (A12), so capping it per generator or including binned Λ as a design coordinate involves no post-treatment conditioning", with the recipe "bin it; stratify randomization on the bin; verify that within a bin, message length no longer predicts Y".
why_wrong: Λ is a deterministic function of the realized treatment, i.e. post-randomization, not pre-treatment; "pre-outcome" is the correct word and it does not license the claim. Worse, operationally: stratifying on the *realized* Λ bin of a drawn message is rejection sampling on the generator's output, which replaces the pinned kernel q_k by q_k(·|Λ∈bin) with an unknown normalizer. That is precisely the entry in the document's own D2 failure catalogue ("best-of-n/rejection sampling/retries (order-statistic factors, unknown normalizers)") and it voids P2's pinned-kernel well-posedness and A6/A9's by-construction status in exactly the arms designed to control leakage — the arms the leakage story depends on.
minimal_repair: Distinguish the two operations explicitly: (i) build separate pinned generators at prescribed leakage levels (the graded redaction series) — legitimate, keeps exact propensities; (ii) conditioning on realized Λ — declare it a re-specified estimand on a selected sub-support with a no-longer-known propensity, and exclude it from the confirmatory analysis. Delete "no post-treatment conditioning".

claim: T13/T14: coarsen (Y,C,N) lexicographically, set Ỹ = 2G_0(u(Z)) − 1 against a prespecified reference, and "T8 and T9 apply verbatim with Y replaced by Ỹ"; sold as "scale-free in Y,C,N (no hand-tuned λ)".
why_wrong: G_0 is the reference arm's mid-rank CDF, an unknown functional of P. Plugging Ĝ_0 puts an estimated nuisance inside the outcome, so T9(i)'s exact unbiasedness — the document's own selling point #3, "exactly unbiased for any outcome model whatsoever" — is lost precisely for the objective §7 recommends; what remains is a U-statistic with an extra influence-function term (which T14 half-acknowledges, then contradicts with "verbatim"). And the stated motivation is hollow: T8 itself shows λ is a budget price identified by LP duality, and the project has a measured budget in GPU seconds and tokens (docs/measured_calibration.md), so λ is pinned by the design rather than hand-tuned. The apparatus buys a reference-dependent, non-transitive objective with an admitted OPEN differentiability problem in exchange for avoiding a parameter that is already determined.
minimal_repair: Demote §7's T13/T14 to an appendix-level secondary reporting device, delete "verbatim" (state the extra Ĝ_0 term and that exact unbiasedness does not survive), and make the primary objective E[Y^π − λC^π] with λ read off the measured budget — reporting degradation (first-correct-then-wrong) separately, as audits.md A3 requires.

claim: §0.2 item 4: "Every treatment is a shippable mechanism... The estimand corresponds to a deployable protocol, in the target-trial sense, which is what makes it auditable by randomized implementation."
location: §0.2 item 4; contradicted by §12 item 3 and §10 "Real humans in the loop (P31)"
why_wrong: In D1 the treatment is a generator of the *user's* messages, executed by a simulated user. No product ships a mechanism that writes its users' turns; §12 item 3 concedes exactly this ("Known propensities are purchased by replacing the human") and P31 concedes that the human-facing analogue is an ITT suggestion estimand. So the target-trial framing applies only to the coordinates that are genuinely product-side: STOP/continuation, interface and rendering variants, and suggestion policies. Those are also the only coordinates the project's measured evidence values (+4.6 pp from stopping decisions alone, audits.md A3).
minimal_repair: Restrict the shippability/target-trial claim to the product-side coordinates by name, and state in §0.1 that message-generator arms are a *measurement* device for blips, not a deployable protocol.

claim: T20(c) and the verdict: "a union bound of an LCB on V(π) with a UCB on V(e) certifies strict improvement over the natural/logging policy" — reported as "a certified strict improvement over the logging policy" among D1's deliverables.
why_wrong: In D1 there is no natural policy in the data: the harness replaced the user, so e is the analyst's own δ-floored randomizer. Certifying that a learned argmax beats a near-uniform mixture over your own arms is close to automatic whenever any two arms differ, and carries no product meaning. "natural/logging policy" silently fuses two different objects — the human's behaviour (absent in D1) and the design's randomizer (present but uninteresting).
minimal_repair: Split the terms. Drop "natural" from T20(c). Pre-register a substantive comparator as a fixed arm — the existing self-check loop, "always continue to the cap", and single-shot — and certify against it with unweighted means on both sides, which needs no importance weights and no clipping at all.

claim: The document's motivating pathology (§1: a naive regression "learns the wrong sign"; "adjustment recovers the truth") and its framing of the machinery as the route to π* and to better decisions (§0.1, §0.2 items 3 and 6, verdict).
location: §1 "The confounding structure we are correcting"; §0.2; verdict
why_wrong: The project's own pre-existing evidence contradicts the decision-level reading, and the theory document does not carry it. docs/premise_findings.md: C1 (unadjusted comparisons invert the ranking) confirmed 0/40, but C3 ("a correlational critic conditioning on the full observed state makes worse decisions") is "Refuted as stated" — a plain state-conditioned critic recovered the exact optimal regime 39/40, mean regret 0.0010; three attempts to break it with latent confounding moved regret by at most 0.030; and known-propensity IPW repaired the residual "only partly and non-monotonically" (0.046→0.033, 0.028→0.028, 0.017→0.019 — one cell got worse). The dominant decision-level error was myopia, which "loses under randomization too — this is not a confounding failure at all". So relative to plain supervised learning plus a randomized experiment, the causal apparatus changes *reported effect estimates* by a lot and *decisions* by ~0.001–0.03 of value. The §1 example is a 2×2 tabular case that any regression including the state as a covariate fixes; the sentence "adjustment is only available once the treatment has been coarsened" is a statement about having a covariate cell, not about needing this framework.
minimal_repair: Rewrite §0.1 to claim two separable deliverables with their own evidence: (a) honest effect *reporting* from interaction logs, where the failure is dramatic and robust; (b) *action selection*, where the evidence attributes the gain to horizon-aware valuation under randomization — i.e. plain backward induction on randomized data — and where the causal correction is a scoped secondary claim. Add the premise-check numbers and the non-monotone IPW repair to §12 as a limitation, and pre-register a non-myopic correlational critic as the baseline the framework must beat, as premise_findings.md item 3 demands.

claim: §0.3 and T26: "without structure, optimizing over history-dependent regimes needs Ω(K^T) rollouts (T26), which is the formal reason a learned blip estimator is mandatory rather than convenient", and "structure plus backward induction is the only known way past the barrier".
location: §0.3; §9 T26(c) and its closing paragraph; §13(b) item 9
why_wrong: Non sequitur, and the lower bound is for a setting the design does not inhabit. The needle-in-a-haystack construction lower-bounds exhaustive search over *history-indexed* regimes with no state abstraction; the document then immediately models nuisances on a summary φ(H_t) (§5, "State representation"), under which dynamic programming costs O(K·T·|S|). A learned blip estimator does not evade the bound — it adds a function-class assumption, which §5 and the T7 caveat elsewhere concede "becomes an identifying assumption and must be labelled as such". Calling it "mandatory" converts an assumption into a theorem.
minimal_repair: Restate as: exhaustive history-indexed search is infeasible, therefore structure must be imposed, and every guarantee downstream is conditional on that structure. Move T26(c) to a remark; it changes no design decision, since no one proposed exhaustive search.

claim: P22's reporting device: "at most X points of quality are recoverable by any implementable stopping rule; our learned rule recovers Y of them", plus the invocation of "the i.i.d. constant ≈0.745".
why_wrong: The paragraph above it proves the unrestricted claim false (its own counterexample: value 1 against a bound of 0.01) and restricts the sandwich to the *truncated* rule τ' = min(τ,T). The reporting sentence then re-asserts the unrestricted version — "any implementable stopping rule" — which is exactly what was just withdrawn, and it is the interesting case (continue where the natural user stopped). Separately, the 0.745 prophet constant is for i.i.d. values; ψ(H_1),…,ψ(H_T) is a dependent, non-stationary adapted sequence, so the constant has no bearing and its citation is decorative.
minimal_repair: Write the device as "...by any stopping rule that never continues past the natural horizon", and delete the 0.745 reference or replace it with a statement for dependent sequences (there is none of comparable strength).

claim: §0.2 item 1: the primary route "is the only route that removes the central obstacle without an untestable assumption".
why_wrong: As written this reads as a global claim and is false. D1 still rests on A11 outcome validity (the document's own "main residual threat"), A12 leakage-proxy adequacy (with the proxy-to-ideal relation admitted "unsigned"), A22 where humans appear, and the A1/A2 channels the document itself lists as live — cache sharing, batch nondeterminism, shared budget pools, temperature-0 non-determinism (§12 item 13, §9 closing). What is actually removed is one untestable assumption, A19, on one coordinate.
minimal_repair: Narrow to: "it removes the exclusion restriction A19 and the positivity obstacle by construction; the remaining untestable assumptions are A11, A12 and the A1/A2 hygiene channels."

claim: P10: "Since α_t grows in t: spend the branching budget late, where the weights have already degenerated."
why_wrong: α_t = E[W²_{1:t}]σ²_{Q,t}. Under the recommended override depth d ≤ 2 with deviations at early turns, E[W²_{1:t}] is flat for t > d, while σ²_{Q,t} typically *shrinks* late (less remaining trajectory randomness). So α_t need not grow, and the allocation rule m_t ∝ sqrt(α_t/c_t) can point early. The prescription rests on an unverified monotonicity.
minimal_repair: State the condition (α_t increasing in t) and make the allocation empirical: estimate α_t and c_t in the pilot and allocate by the formula rather than by the slogan.

claim: §5 T9(v) and §15 item 1: "OPEN: whether knowing e lowers the longitudinal efficiency bound... we decline to assert the longitudinal statement."
why_wrong: This is essentially settled in the longitudinal literature the document already cites: the score of the treatment mechanism is orthogonal to the efficient influence function for the g-formula parameter, so the efficiency bound is the same whether the sequential randomization probabilities are known or not (van der Laan–Robins). Listing it as an open problem inflates §15 and makes the caution look strategic rather than substantive.
minimal_repair: Replace with the standard statement and a citation, noting that knowing e buys exact unbiasedness and finite-sample validity, not asymptotic efficiency — which is what the document already wants to say.

claim: §13(b) lists twelve "real technical contributions", including (1) the exact second-moment recursion, (2) the curse of description length, (9) the Ω(K^T) query lower bound.
why_wrong: These are short exercises, not contributions: (1) is the tower rule applied to ∏w_t² plus a one-line change of measure; (2) is monotonicity of Rényi divergences composed with the autoregressive KL chain rule, and the conclusion (sequence-level IS over free text is dead) is folklore in the RLHF/OPE literature; (9) is a textbook needle-in-a-haystack. Presenting them alongside genuine items invites an area chair to discount the whole list. Note also that docs/positioning.md already concedes most of the surrounding framing to prior work (Wang AAAI-25, Zhang–Wang–Dhillon, Nakamura–Imai, DeepBlip, DRQ-learner, CPO) and identifies the surviving novelty as the *design*.
minimal_repair: Demote items 1, 2, 9 to "useful accounting identities" in §4, and lead §13(b) with the design claim positioning.md says survives: prospective sequential randomization of an in-conversation intervention with logged propensities, plus branch-sampled validation (T27).

claim: §0.2 item 3: "a cheap badly-calibrated LLM critic carries zero bias risk".
why_wrong: True only for the value functional V(π) under cross-fitting. The critic also selects π̂ (T19, where its error costs value at first order) and supplies the stop decision (T8), and those are the deliverables. Given that the project's headline is a learned stopping rule, critic calibration is exactly what determines what ships.
minimal_repair: Qualify: "carries zero bias risk for the value estimate; its error enters the learned regime at first order through T19".

claim: §8 (P15's judge apparatus, most of P24's judge-bias analysis) presented as a co-equal threat section.
why_wrong: For this project the primary outcome is programmatic (hidden-test pass, A1-audited with the visible/hidden split), so the judge machinery governs no primary number. What has teeth is narrower: P24(ii)'s selection optimism from a shared stopping/scoring channel, and channel separation. The rest is ceremony relative to the planned experiment.
minimal_repair: Compress §8 to: channel separation, selection/evaluation splitting, the horizon-invariance calibration test, and a one-line pointer for the case where a judge is ever used as a secondary outcome.

location: A6 (§2 table) + §16 item 3 + P5 "Bounded case" + T20(d)
claim: A randomization floor e_t(k|H_t) ≥ δ with δ ≥ 0.25, combined with "about 5–6 effective classes per decision point", yielding E[W²] ≤ δ^(-d) = 16 at d = 2, n_eff ≥ nδ^d, and ≈5×10⁴ conversations to certify a 0.05 gap.
why_wrong: A uniform floor over m arms requires mδ ≤ Σ_k e_t(k|h) = 1, i.e. δ ≤ 1/m. With m = 5–6 the largest attainable floor is 0.2–0.167, and δ = 0.25 is feasible only for m ≤ 4. Every headline variance and sample-size figure in the document is evaluated at an arithmetically unattainable floor. At the feasible δ = 1/6 and d = 2, M = δ^(-2) = 36, not 16, so the certificate sample size in T20(d) more than doubles; at d = 3, δ^(-3) = 216 rather than 64. This also propagates into P5's "design knob" table, n_eff ≥ nδ^d, and the §0.2 claim that the machinery "costs roughly what a stratified A/B test costs".
minimal_repair: State δ ≤ 1/m explicitly in A6, and either (a) cap the choke point at m ≤ 4 arms per decision point to keep δ = 0.25, or (b) keep 5–6 arms and recompute all quoted numbers at δ = 1/m (M = 36 at d = 2, n ≳ 2.4×10⁵ for a 0.05 gap). Alternatively define δ as a floor only on the arms the target regimes put mass on, and say so in A6 — but then blips for all library generators are no longer covered.

location: P5 ("override depth"), T19 ("the history-shift factor is bounded here by design"), §10 D1 row ("V(π) and π* over Π_cp with W ≤ δ^{-d}"), T20(d)
claim: Override depth d is a design knob set to d ≤ 2, so weights obey W ≤ δ^{-d} ≤ 16, the history-shift factor in the value-loss propagation is "bounded by design", and the D1 design identifies and certifies V(π) and π* over Π_cp at that weight bound.
why_wrong: d is defined as the number of turns at which π differs from e. The optimal regime produced by T8's backward induction is deterministic at every turn, so for π* (and for essentially every member of a full-depth policy class Π_cp) d = T, not 2, and W ≤ δ^{-T}. With the feasible δ = 1/6 and T = 5 this is 7776, and even at δ = 0.25, T = 5 it is 1024. T20(d)'s linear-in-M rate then requires n ≳ M log(|Π|/α)/gap² ≈ 10⁷ trajectories for a 0.05 gap on a learned full-depth regime, against the advertised 5×10⁴. The "genuine advantage over settings with unbounded ratios" in T19 is therefore exponential in T exactly where the document uses it, and the D1 row conflates two incompatible targets: shallow-deviation regimes (small d, certifiable) and π* (d = T, not certifiable off-policy at the quoted budget). T7's "honest caveat" gestures at this but the headline claims do not.
minimal_repair: Split the D1 entitlements: (i) depth-d deviation regimes Π_d ⊂ Π_cp, for which W ≤ δ^{-d} and T20 applies with the stated numbers; (ii) π* and other full-depth regimes, whose values must be obtained by on-policy rollout (E7) or by a re-logged policy-iteration step, with off-policy certification explicitly disclaimed. Replace "W ≤ δ^{-d}" in the D1 row with "W ≤ δ^{-d} for depth-d deviations; δ^{-T} for full-depth regimes", and re-derive T19's history-shift constant accordingly.

location: T13/T14 (§7), "Then T8 and T9 apply verbatim with Y replaced by Ỹ"; A17; §0.2 item 3
claim: The prioritized outcome reduces to a bounded pseudo-outcome Ỹ = 2G₀(u(Z)) − 1 ∈ [−1,1] such that T8's backward induction and T9's sequential DR "apply verbatim with Y replaced by Ỹ", the STOP arm's value remains known, and sequential DR is exactly unbiased for any outcome model whatsoever.
why_wrong: G₀ is the mid-rank CDF of u(Z) under the reference regime π₀ — an unknown functional of P that must be estimated, and (unless π₀ = e) off-policy estimated with its own weights from the same data used for the ψ-estimate. So (a) Ỹ is not an observed outcome but a plug-in Ĝ₀-transform, i.e. double dipping: E[ψ̂] = ψ fails, because an outcome-law nuisance now enters the remainder, destroying the "exactly unbiased for any Q̂" headline that §0.2 item 3 and the closing verdict rest on; (b) Q_t(H_t,STOP) is no longer a known deterministic functional of H_t, since it requires G₀, so T8's central asymmetry ("the stop arm's value is known") is lost; (c) π* becomes the argmax of an estimated objective, compounding the exceptional-law non-regularity. The document contradicts itself two paragraphs later by correctly giving the two-term EIF φ_π[G₀⁻] + φ_{π₀}[Ḡ_π] — a two-term EIF is precisely the statement that T9 does *not* apply verbatim.
minimal_repair: Either (i) estimate G₀ on an independent, pre-registered pilot sample (or a held-out fold never used for the value estimate) and declare Ỹ a fixed measurable transform — then T8/T9 really do apply verbatim; or (ii) keep G₀ as a nuisance, use the stated two-term EIF, state the bilinear remainder in (Ĝ₀ − G₀, Q̂ − Q) and the product-rate condition it requires, and downgrade §0.2 item 3 and §13(b) item 5 from "exactly unbiased" to "doubly robust with a second-order remainder" for the prioritized estimand.

location: A18 (§2 table, "needed only where e is estimated"; §10 ladder row "A18 rates: vacuous"), T9(i)–(ii), E1 (TMLE variant)
claim: A18 (cross-fitting; corrected cross-term product rate) is "vacuous in D1" because e is known; with e known, E[ψ̂] = ψ for any Q̂ whatsoever; and cross-fitted one-step *or* TMLE both deliver this.
why_wrong: Two distinct conditions are collapsed into one. The *rate* condition is indeed vacuous when e is known; the *sample-splitting* condition is not. Exact unbiasedness of the sequential DR estimator requires Q̂ to be independent of the evaluation fold; if Q̂ is fit on the same data, E[ψ̂] ≠ ψ even with e known exactly, and the CLT's empirical-process/stability term (P_n − P)(φ_Q̂ − φ_{Q^∞}) = o_P(n^{-1/2}) also relies on fold independence. Separately, the TMLE listed as a co-primary in E1 fits the fluctuation parameter on the same data it evaluates in order to solve the EIF equation, so it is *not* exactly unbiased (O(1/n) bias); neither are E4's clipped IPW (biased by construction) nor any self-normalized variant. Marking A18 "vacuous" in the assumption table licenses exactly the implementation that voids the document's headline robustness claim.
minimal_repair: Split A18 into A18a (cross-fitting / sample splitting: required in every design, including D1) and A18b (product rate on (ê, Q̂): required only where e is estimated), and mark only A18b vacuous in D1. Restrict the "exactly unbiased for any outcome model" claim in T9(i), §0.2 item 3 and the verdict to the cross-fitted one-step/AIPW estimator, and add one sentence that TMLE, clipped IPW and self-normalized versions trade exactness for other properties.

location: §5 "Cross-fitting scheme" ("Additional clustering for standard errors by time block and model-version epoch") vs A2 (§2 table) and §12.9
claim: Standard errors should be clustered by time block and model-version epoch, with arms randomized within time blocks so residual provider drift is "balanced rather than confounded".
