why_wrong: A2 states that violation of the frozen-receiver condition makes the estimand *undefined, not noisy*, and §12.9 states that all uncertainty is conditional on one frozen receiver and that reporting SEs appearing to cover generalization across model versions would be misleading. Clustering variance by model-version epoch does exactly that: it treats snapshot drift as a random component of sampling error, i.e. as noise around a single well-defined parameter — which is only coherent if the estimand is redefined as an average over a population of snapshots. It cannot be both. Compounding this, cluster-robust inference with a handful of epochs is invalid on its own terms (few-cluster bias), so the prescription is not even a conservative fix.
minimal_repair: Pick one regime and state it: (a) A2 holds — report separate estimates per pinned snapshot, cluster only by task family and time block, and delete model-version epoch as a clustering level; or (b) define the estimand as E over a declared snapshot distribution, admit A2 is relaxed, and use a design with enough epochs (plus a small-cluster correction, e.g. CR2/t(G−1)) to support it.

location: P5b (§5), and §16 item 4 ("wide-shallow training slice (n_b = 1 paired contrast)")
claim: With Var(β̂) ∝ (σ_e²/n_b + σ_m²)/n and budget B ∝ n(c₀ + n_b), the variance "(given σ_m² > 0) is increasing in n_b once the budget is substituted", so for fitting a blip model the budget-optimal design is the widest one, n_b = 1.
why_wrong: Substituting n = B/(c₀ + n_b) gives f(n_b) = (σ_e²/n_b + σ_m²)(c₀ + n_b) = σ_e²c₀/n_b + σ_e² + σ_m²c₀ + σ_m²n_b, whose derivative is σ_m² − σ_e²c₀/n_b². f is therefore *decreasing* on n_b < σ_e√c₀/σ_m and only then increasing: the optimum is interior at n_b* = σ_e√c₀/σ_m, not at the boundary. The monotone-increasing claim holds only in the c₀ = 0 special case, which contradicts the document's own cost model — and the errata (§14, Route D) records B ∝ n(c₀ + n_b) as a deliberately carried correction. Since the roll-in cost of a multi-turn conversation is substantial and branch outcome noise σ_e is large relative to blip heterogeneity σ_m in exactly the regime the paper expects (small effects), n_b* > 1 is the likely case, so the §16 design recommendation is probably inverted.
minimal_repair: Replace the conclusion with n_b* = max(1, σ_e√c₀/σ_m), state that n_b = 1 is optimal only when c₀ ≤ σ_m²/σ_e², and make the training-slice width in §16 item 4 conditional on a pilot estimate of σ_e², σ_m² and c₀.

location: P12 (§7, "the extrema are not attained at the comonotone/antimonotone couplings, so no Fréchet–Hoeffding closed form is available in general (the draft's scalar reduction is withdrawn)"), §15 item 6, §14 Route E
claim: Because c(v,w) = 1{v > w} is neither supermodular nor submodular, the sharp bounds on within-unit win probability must be computed as an optimal-transport LP; no closed form exists, and closed-form sharp bounds for lexicographic comparisons are an open problem.
why_wrong: Non-supermodularity correctly rules out the comonotone coupling as the maximizer, but it does not imply that no closed form exists. 1{v > w} = 1{v − w > 0}, and sharp bounds on the distribution function of a difference with fixed marginals are the classical Makarov (1981) / Rüschendorf (1982) bounds — closed-form, attained at explicitly constructible (shuffle) couplings: sup_couplings P(V > W) = 1 − sup_t {F_V(t) − F_W(t)}⁺ and inf_couplings P(V > W) = sup_t {F_W(t) − F_V(t)}⁺ (up to one-sided limits). The document cites Makarov, Rüschendorf and Fan–Park in §13(a) and then declares the problem LP-only, so it over-corrects against itself. Because T13 already reduces the lexicographic comparison to a *scalar* u(Z), the scalar-difference bound applies directly and §15 item 6 is not open.
minimal_repair: Reinstate a closed form: report the Makarov/Rüschendorf sharp interval for P(u(Z^π) > u(Z^{π₀})) in terms of the two estimated marginal CDFs of u, note that the maximizer is a shuffle rather than the comonotone coupling, and delete "closed-form sharp transport bounds for three-level lexicographic comparisons" from the open list (keep only the vector-valued, non-scalarizable case if you want an open item).

location: T9(v) (§5, "OPEN: whether knowing e lowers the longitudinal efficiency bound ... we decline to assert the longitudinal statement"), §15 item 1
claim: Whether knowledge of the randomization probabilities lowers the longitudinal semiparametric efficiency bound for ψ = V(π) is open; only robustness and finite-sample validity are claimed.
why_wrong: It is answerable in two lines from the EIF the document already displays. Write φ = V₁(H₁) − ψ + Σ_t W_{1:t}(V_{t+1} − Q_t). Its projection onto the turn-t treatment tangent space is E[φ | H_t, K_t] − E[φ | H_t]; the turn-t residual has conditional mean zero given (H_t, K_t), all later residuals have conditional mean zero, and all earlier terms plus V₁ are H_t-measurable, so the difference is identically 0. Hence φ has zero component in ⊕_t T_{A_t}. Removing that subspace (which is exactly what knowing e does) leaves φ still an influence function lying in the reduced tangent space, so φ is the EIF in both models and Var(φ) is the bound in both: knowing e does *not* lower the longitudinal bound for a fixed π. Declining to assert a statement that follows from one's own EIF is a gap, not caution — and it leaves §0.2 item 3's "exact inverse of the situation in medical DTR analysis" rhetorically unmoored.
minimal_repair: State and prove the tangent-space orthogonality above, conclude the Hahn (1998) analogue does hold for V(π) with fixed π, and narrow the OPEN flag to functionals for which it genuinely fails or is unknown — MSM parameters indexed by e, V(π*) under exceptional laws, and the P-dependent tilt regime of T30 whose intervention itself depends on P.

location: T8 (§4, "λ is a budget price, not a hyperparameter") vs T20 (§6), T9 (§5), T13 (§7), A10
claim: A budget-constrained optimum equals the unpenalized optimum of E[Y^π − λC^π] for some λ ≥ 0 by LP duality, so λ is a budget price rather than a hyperparameter; and T20 gives a finite-sample lower bound on V(π) with Y − λC ∈ [0,1].
why_wrong: The dual multiplier is a functional of P: it is determined by the supporting hyperplane of the convex hull of *attainable* (value, cost) pairs, which is unknown and must be estimated from the same data. Every downstream statement that treats Y − λC as a fixed bounded outcome therefore involves a data-dependent estimand: T20's empirical-Bernstein bound is no longer a valid 1−α certificate for a fixed parameter (λ̂ is selected after seeing the data), the EIF in T9 omits the influence contribution of λ̂, and the prioritized reduction in T13 inherits the same problem. This is the same double-dipping failure mode as G₀ in T13, one level up. It appears nowhere in §12 or §15.
minimal_repair: Either pre-register λ on a grid and report the whole frontier with a union bound over the grid (λ then *is* a hyperparameter, and say so), or keep the dual reading and add λ̂'s influence-function contribution plus a post-selection correction; in the latter case T20 must be restated as a bound holding simultaneously over the λ-grid.

claim: If the stopping rule is chosen to maximize the estimated value, the apparent gain over the truth is Θ(σ√log K̄) even when true quality is flat, which "at realistic judge noise and K̄ ≈ 5 is comparable to any real effect this project hopes to report".
why_wrong: The rate omits the replicate/sample factor that P11 correctly retains (P11: σ√(2 log K/n_b)). For a rule selected by maximizing an estimated value across n independent trajectories, the relevant noise scale is σ/√n, so the selection inflation is O(σ√(log K̄ / n)) and vanishes — it is not comparable to a fixed effect size. The non-vanishing quantity is a different object: the within-unit optimistic bias E[ε_τ] of P24(i), which persists as n → ∞ because the same realized judge noise both triggers the stop and scores the outcome. As written, the two are conflated, and the §12.7 and §15.7 framings inherit the conflation, which misdirects the proposed remedy (independent channels fix the within-unit bias; sample size fixes the selection inflation).
minimal_repair: Write the selection inflation as Θ(σ√(log K̄ / n_h)) with n_h the number of independent scorings per decision node (n_h = 1 for per-trajectory argmax, n_h = n for a global rule selected across units), and present P24(i)'s E[ε_τ] separately as the bias that does not average away. Keep the "comparable to real effects" warning only for the n_h = 1 case.

location: T29 (§11.2, "point-identified — it is simply not regularly estimable"), §12 item 1 ("never estimable"), §14 Route A ("resolved by the identified-but-irregularly-estimable reading")
claim: The canonical-message (fixed-text) value is point-identified but "not regularly estimable", with effective sample size of order n·e^{−Θ(m)}; the T·ρ band is a "finite-sample/irregularity band". This reading is presented as the resolution of the Route-A Thm 5 vs Thm 2 contradiction.
why_wrong: Irregularity is a precise property — non-existence of a pathwise-differentiable representation with finite variance bound, hence no √n-consistent estimator. Under the document's own conditions (countable L, full-support softmax, absolute continuity), the functional E[Y(a)] has the ordinary AIPW influence function with variance bounded by E[1/g(a|X)], which is finite whenever g(a|X) > 0 a.s. and E[1/g] < ∞. It is therefore *regularly* estimable at √n with an efficiency bound of order e^{Θ(m)} — a catastrophic constant, not an irregularity. Genuine irregularity requires E[1/g(a|X)] = ∞ (the Khan–Tamer weak-overlap regime the document cites but does not invoke here). Using "irregular" as a synonym for "huge variance" makes the errata's headline resolution technically false, and "never estimable" in §12.1 is wrong as stated.
minimal_repair: Replace "not regularly estimable" with "regularly estimable with semiparametric efficiency bound of order e^{Θ(m)}", state the AIPW influence function and its variance bound, and add the separate, checkable condition E[1/g(a|X)] = ∞ as the one under which genuine irregularity (Khan–Tamer) obtains. Relabel the T·ρ object as a finite-sample variance band, dropping "irregularity".

location: P10 (§5, branch-augmented DR variance and budget allocation)
claim: Var ≈ Σ_t [E[W²_{1:t}]σ²_{Q,t}/m_t + E[W²_{1:t−1}]σ²_{V,t}/m′_t] + V₀, with independent optimal allocations m_t ∝ √(α_t/c_t), m′_t analogously.
why_wrong: The two "noise sources" are not independent when the same branch rollouts are used for both. V̂_t(H_t) = Σ_k π_t(k|H_t) Q̂_t(H_t,k) contains the arm-K_t rollout mean that also constitutes Q̂_t(H_t,K_t), and the two enter the influence function with opposite signs at weights W_{1:t−1} and W_{1:t}. This induces a cross term of order −2 π_t(K_t|H_t) E[W_{1:t−1}W_{1:t}] σ²_{Q,t}/m_t that the additive display omits, so the stated variance is neither exact nor a bound in general, and the separate allocation over (m_t, m′_t) double-counts the shared rollouts. The corrected two-noise-source claim is listed as a technical contribution (§13(b) item 7), so the omission matters.
minimal_repair: Specify the rollout design: either draw disjoint rollout sets for Q̂_t(H_t,K_t) and for V̂_t(H_t) (then the additive formula is exact and both allocations are separate), or use shared rollouts and add the cross-covariance term before solving the Lagrangian — the optimum shifts, and the "spend the budget late" conclusion should be re-checked under the corrected α_t.

location: §0.4 table, Ext-B row ("no exclusion restriction; the weight is a scalar observable normalizer; the EIF collapses (T30)"), §11.1
claim: Ext-B buys a message-level estimand with no exclusion restriction, an exactly two-sided doubly robust estimator, and an EIF with no action-level text critic; its price is listed as mechanism-relativity, bundling, and a KL budget.
why_wrong: The price column omits the binding statistical cost. Z_t(θ,h) = E_P[e^{θ′φ}|H_t = h] is a conditional expectation over a long, never-repeating text history — an infinite-dimensional, P-dependent nuisance that appears inside the intervention itself. Root-n inference for Ext-B therefore rests entirely on the product rate ‖Ẑ − Z‖·‖Q̃̂ − Q̃‖ = o_P(n^{-1/2}) for two text-history regressions, which §12.12 and §15.2 concede is unverifiable and has no smoothness theory. Unlike D1, there is no known-propensity fallback: if Ẑ is inconsistent the estimator is inconsistent, E[w_t|H_t] = Z_t/Ẑ_t ≠ 1 so the exact P-martingale property and the E[w_t|H_t] = 1 specification check both fail, and the Ville-type anytime-valid certificate floated in §15.3 is unavailable. The route trades an untestable *identification* assumption (A19) for an unverifiable *estimation* condition, and the table presents only one side of that trade.
minimal_repair: Add to the Ext-B price column: "√n inference requires a product rate on two text-history nuisances (the conditional normalizer Z_t and the tilted critic), unverifiable per §12.12, with no known-propensity fallback; with estimated Z_t the martingale and E[w|H] = 1 properties are approximate." Also state whether Z_t is cross-fitted, since it is estimated from the same data as the value.

location: T28 (§28, term 3: "a history-shift / transport term ... which is not estimable") vs P14b and A13
claim: The third term of the sim-to-real decomposition, the shift between S-coarsened history laws, is not estimable and must be carried as a named sensitivity parameter or bounded by an assumed density ratio; hence "one estimable term, one mix-relative term, and one unestimable transport term".
why_wrong: The identity rolls in under H_t ~ P^U, and P^U is exactly what human logs provide. Under A13 (reset fidelity) the simulator's continuation can be rolled out from a *real logged prefix* — the mechanism P14b already establishes as executable — so E_{H_t ~ P^U}[∫(U_t − Û_t)Q^Û_t] needs no density ratio between coarsened history laws at all: you replay the real prefix and branch. What remains genuinely unestimable is narrower (histories the logs never reach, and stale-reference/replay-fidelity error), not the transport term wholesale. The over-claim is conservative but inconsistent, and it is advertised as a contribution (§13(b) item 10).
minimal_repair: Restate term 3 as "estimable by replaying logged human prefixes into the harness under A13, up to replay fidelity and up to histories outside the logs' support; unestimable only for π-reachable real histories the logs never visit", and move the sensitivity parameter to that residual.

claim: With δ = 0.25, d ≤ 2 (M = 16), |Π| = 100, α = 0.05: about 5×10⁴ conversations to certify a 0.05 gap, 1.2×10⁴ for 0.10, and 1.2×10⁴ for a single-turn design at M = 4.
why_wrong: The three numbers are internally consistent (they scale as M/gap²) but the base constant is optimistic. Using the document's own bound Ê[min(W,M)²] ≤ M and a union bound over |Π| plus the separate UCB on V(e) required by T20(c), the half-width is ≈ √(2M log(2|Π|/α)/n) with log(4000) ≈ 8.3, and the gap must cover both one-sided bounds: n ≈ 8M log(2|Π|/α)/gap² ≈ 4×10⁵ at M = 16, gap = 0.05 — roughly 2–8× the quoted figure depending on how the gap is split. The §0.2 claim that the machinery "costs roughly what a stratified A/B test over the m arms costs" depends on this constant.
minimal_repair: Write the explicit constant, state how the gap is allocated between the LCB on V(π) and the UCB on V(e), and requote the three figures (or present them as order-of-magnitude with the constant left symbolic).

claim: Asymptotic variance Var(φ(Y_J))/n + Var(we)/|V|, so the |V| term binds only when the influence-weighted judge error has non-negligible variance.
why_wrong: The display treats the two terms as independent, which holds only when the validation set V is drawn separately from the n units used for the judge-based estimate. In the design described ("arm-by-arm validation" within the same run, §16 item 5), V ⊂ the n, so there is a covariance term between φ(Y_J) on V and the correction, and a finite-population factor of order (1 − |V|/n). Cross-fitting w_i removes the nuisance-induced dependence but not the overlap.
minimal_repair: Either sample V disjointly from the estimation sample and say so, or add the covariance term and the (1 − |V|/n) factor to the variance expression.

location: P5 (§4, "Cov(w_t², χ²_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) | H_t) ≠ 0"); T29 ("δ^{-1} in place of e^{Θ(m)}"); T7 ("effective sample size of order nδ/T"); T9(ii) ("plus E[W²Q̂²] < ∞")
claim: Four small technical statements supporting the variance accounting.
why_wrong: (a) The obstruction to factoring the recursion is Cov(w_t², Γ_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) | H_t), not Cov(w_t², χ²_{t+1}) — Γ_{t+1} is the forward second-moment factor, and writing χ²_{t+1} makes the stated reason not match the displayed recursion. (b) T29's coarse indicator ratio is a product over t, so the bound is δ^{-d} (or δ^{-T}), not δ^{-1}. (c) The blip ESS nδ/T ignores P(T ≥ s): with an endogenous horizon, later turns are reached far less often, so the turn-s ESS is of order n δ P(T ≥ s)/E[T]. (d) E[W²Q̂²] < ∞ is implied by W ≤ δ^{-d} and bounded Q̂ and so is vacuous; the condition that actually binds for the CLT is L₂ convergence of Q̂ to a fixed limit *under the weighted measure* W_{1:t}·P, which is stronger than under P and is the version that should be stated given §12.12.
minimal_repair: Replace χ²_{t+1} with Γ_{t+1} in P5; write δ^{-d} in T29; add the P(T ≥ s) factor in T7; and in T9(ii) drop the moment condition in favour of "‖Q̂_t − Q_t^∞‖_{L₂(W_{1:t}·P)} = o_P(1) with Q̂ fold-independent".

location: §1 ("adjustment is only available once the treatment has been coarsened, because at the fine level there is no cell to adjust within"); E2 (§5)
claim: Confounding adjustment requires coarsening because the fine (text) level has no cell to adjust within; and the g-estimation equation uses U_it(β) = Y_i − Σ_{s≥t} γ_s(...).
why_wrong: (a) The claim conflates nonparametric within-cell stratification with adjustment. The document's own DR/critic machinery adjusts at the fine level without any cell — Q̂_t(H_t, ·) is a regression, not a stratification — and the tilt route (T30) adjusts on a scalar feature with no coarsening at all. The motivational sentence therefore argues against the paper's own primary route. (b) E2's blipped-down residual uses Y_i where the value estimand is Y − λC, and imposing isotonic constraints along ordered axes gives β̂ non-standard (boundary/cube-root-type) asymptotics whenever the constraint binds, which is unremarked.
minimal_repair: (a) Restate as "nonparametric within-stratum adjustment requires coarsening; model-based adjustment does not, which is why the fine level needs either a critic (D1) or a scalar feature (Ext-B)". (b) Write U_it(β) = (Y_i − λC_i) − Σ_{s≥t} γ_s(...) and add a sentence on inference under active isotonic constraints (e.g. report the unconstrained fit alongside, or use a projection-based interval).

claim: A6: "Randomization floor e_t(k|H_t) >= delta (recommend delta >= 0.25)", together with §16.3 "about 5-6 effective classes per decision point, floor delta >= 0.25" and §0.1 "|K| = m finite ... STOP is one of the selectors". T20(d) and P5 then use M = delta^{-d} = 16 at delta = 0.25.
location: A6 (§2 table); §16.3 item 3; P5 "Bounded case"; T20(d)
why_wrong: A uniform floor over all m selectors requires m*delta <= 1, i.e. m <= 1/delta = 4. With 5-6 generator classes plus STOP (m = 6 or 7) the maximum attainable uniform floor is 1/6 ≈ 0.167, and no design can satisfy delta >= 0.25. The floor cannot be restricted to "only the arms pi uses" either, because pi* is learned over history-dependent rules and may select any arm at any history, so coverage must hold for all k. Every downstream number that depends on delta = 0.25 is therefore unattainable at the recommended taxonomy size: M = delta^{-2} = 16 becomes 36, n_eff >= n*delta^d falls by 2.25x, and T20(d)'s headline 5x10^4 conversations for a 0.05 gap becomes ≈1.1x10^5.
minimal_repair: State the constraint m <= 1/delta explicitly in A6 and pick one branch: either cap the choke point at m <= 4 (3 generators + STOP) and keep delta = 0.25, or set delta = 1/m (0.167 at m = 6) and recompute M, n_eff, and all T20(d) sample sizes from that value. If a non-uniform floor is wanted, define A6 as a floor only on a pre-registered sub-library that Pi_cp is restricted to, and say so wherever delta^{-d} appears.

claim: T3's proof: "The trajectory laws under e and pi share P_X, every generator kernel q_k, and every receiver kernel M ... In the ratio of densities the q_k and M factors cancel, leaving the displayed selector ratio." A5 lists "pinned, pre-registered, version-hashed generator library" as BC, and P2 concludes "assign generator k names a fully specified stochastic intervention, because q_k is a pinned kernel."
why_wrong: The cancellation requires q_k to be a kernel in the recorded H_t alone and, crucially, to be conditionally independent of the selector history K_{1:t-1} given H_t. A simulated user implemented as an LLM with any cross-turn hidden state - a carried KV cache, a persona/scratchpad not written into H_t, hidden reasoning tokens discarded each turn, a persistent tool or memory handle - has action kernel q_{K_t}(· | H_t, U_t) with U_t a function of K_{1:t-1}. Then the trajectory density does not factor as (selector terms) x (common q and M terms): the hidden state is post-treatment with respect to earlier selectors and mediates them, so the q factors differ between the e-law and the pi-law and do not cancel. P2's well-posedness argument collapses at the same point, because "assign generator k" no longer names a fixed kernel. Note the document's own D2 catalogue treats discarded chain-of-thought as "pre-treatment generation randomness, not a mediator, so ignorability survives and only computability fails" - that is true for a within-turn scratchpad and false for state carried across turns, which is exactly the default implementation of a multi-turn LLM user.
minimal_repair: Add to A5 an explicit statelessness condition: every generator call at turn t is made from a fresh context constructed deterministically from the recorded H_t (no carried cache, no persona memory, no cross-turn scratchpad), verified by an input-provenance hash of the rendered generator prompt. Add the check to §16's hygiene list. If cross-turn state is unavoidable, redefine the history to include it (H_t must contain U_t), and note that A9 (phi-measurable propensity) and the "no text critic" claims must then be restated on the enlarged history.

claim: §1: "pi* = argmax over Pi_cp of V(pi) over choke-point-measurable policies"; T8: "V*_t(H_t) = max{Q_t(H_t,STOP), max_{k != STOP} Q_t(H_t,k)}, with the optimal regime read off the argmax"; §5 "State representation. Histories grow, so nuisances must be modelled on a summary"; T20(d) certifies with M = delta^{-d}, d <= 2, |Pi| = 100.
why_wrong: Two distinct defects, both about which sigma-algebra Pi_cp lives on, and neither is resolved anywhere. (i) "Choke-point-measurable" is never defined as a sigma-algebra. If Pi_cp = sigma(H_t)-measurable rules on verbatim text histories, T8's backward induction is valid but every Q_t must be evaluated at atoms of probability e^{-Theta(mt)} visited once, and max over such a class has optimism equal to the outcome's full range. If Pi_cp = sigma(phi(H_t))-measurable rules, then T8's Bellman recursion is simply invalid: the optimum over a restricted (non-sufficient) policy class does not satisfy a Bellman equation, and backward induction on phi-measurable value functions returns the greedy-in-restricted-class rule, not argmax_{Pi_cp} V. This is the standard failure of dynamic programming under a coarsened state, and it is not covered by T9's "exactly unbiased for any Q-hat" - that robustness is a property of *evaluating* a fixed pi, not of *optimizing*. (ii) The certificate's arithmetic is for a different class than pi*. T20(d) uses d <= 2 so M = 16; but a history-dependent pi* from T8 deviates at every turn, so its override depth is d = T and M = delta^{-T} = 4^5 = 1024 at delta = 0.25, T = 5 - requiring n ≈ 1024*log(|Pi|/alpha)/gap^2 ≈ 3x10^6 conversations for a 0.05 gap, sixty times the advertised figure. And |Pi| = 100 is a finite pre-registered candidate set; Pi_cp as defined is not finite, so log|Pi| must be replaced by a complexity term that a learned blip-threshold family does not obviously control.
minimal_repair: Define Pi_cp explicitly as the set of rules measurable with respect to a pre-registered sigma(phi(H_t)) AND with override depth <= d against e, and state pi* as the maximizer over that restricted class. Then (a) replace T8's DP with an explicit statement that backward induction over phi-measurable Q's targets the unrestricted-class optimum, so either assume phi is sufficient (label it as an identifying assumption, alongside the existing state-representation caveat) or optimize directly over the restricted class by policy search with the T20 certificate; (b) carry M = delta^{-d} with the same d that defines Pi_cp everywhere, and recompute T20(d) for the depth actually used by the reported pi*; (c) replace |Pi| = 100 with the pre-registered candidate count or a covering-number bound.

claim: T13: "With u representing the preorder and G_0 the mid-rank CDF of u(Z) under a prespecified reference pi_0 ... Y-tilde = 2G_0(u(Z)) - 1 in [-1,1]. Then T8 and T9 apply verbatim with Y replaced by Y-tilde; the stop arm's value remains known, because Y_{t-1}, accrued cost and turn count are all components of H_t."
why_wrong: G_0 is the mid-rank CDF of u(Z^{pi_0}) under a *counterfactual regime*, not a known function. Three consequences the document does not carry. (a) The pseudo-outcome is not a function of the unit's observed record: Y-tilde depends on a functional of the law under pi_0, which must itself be identified (its own positivity and exchangeability), so the estimand is defined through a second counterfactual distribution rather than "a bounded terminal outcome". (b) T8's known-stop-arm claim is false: knowing Z at the stop is not knowing 2G_0(u(Z)) - 1, so Q_t(H_t, STOP) becomes a nuisance depending on an estimated G_0, and the advertised "nuisance asymmetry - the stop arm's value is known" (§0.2.5, T8) evaporates for the prioritized objective. (c) T9(i)'s "E[psi-hat] = psi for any Q-hat whatsoever" fails: G_0-hat enters the outcome multiplicatively and non-linearly, so exactness is lost and the estimator's bias is driven by ||G_0-hat - G_0||. The document's own EIF (phi_pi[G_0^-] + phi_{pi_0}[G-bar_pi]) concedes that G_0 estimation contributes an influence-function term - which directly contradicts "T8 and T9 apply verbatim".
minimal_repair: Say explicitly that G_0 is an estimated nuisance and that the prioritized route is doubly robust, not exactly unbiased; use the two-term EIF already given and cross-fit G_0-hat. For T8, either (i) prespecify G_0 as a fixed known transform (e.g. a pre-registered rank function from a pilot, frozen before outcomes are examined), in which case Y-tilde is an ordinary bounded terminal reward, the stop arm is again known, and T8/T9 do apply verbatim - at the cost that the win-probability interpretation is only approximate; or (ii) keep the exact win-probability semantics and replace T8's DP with a fixed-point/plug-in argument that accounts for G_0-hat, and delete "applies verbatim" and "the stop arm's value remains known".

claim: T8: "Q_t(H_t, STOP) is a known deterministic functional of H_t when the decision-time signal is recorded, and otherwise a pure prediction problem with no causal content", plus §0.2.5 "the stopping decision is a scalar blip with a known stop-arm value (T8)". Against A11(d) "independent stopping/scoring channels" and §8's "Requirements, not recommendations: ... two prespecified independent measurement channels, one for stopping and one for scoring".
why_wrong: These cannot both hold. Q_t(H_t, STOP) = psi(H_t) is known only if the outcome scorer's value is itself a recorded component of H_t, i.e. available at decision time and readable by the regime. But §8 requires the stopping channel and the scoring channel to be independent instruments precisely so that the stopping rule does not read the outcome score. Under that requirement, psi is not in H_t, Q_t(H_t, STOP) = E[psi^{(2)} | H_t] is an estimated nuisance, and the whole advertised advantage ("the only causal nuisance is the continuation value ... has no medical analogue") disappears. Worse, the branch the document actually needs for T8 is the one that manufactures P24(ii): if the same scorer supplies both the decision-time signal and the outcome, then T8's argmax over STOP versus continuation is a rule selected to maximize a noisy estimate of the very quantity being reported, and P24(ii)'s own Theta(sigma sqrt(log K-bar)) optimism applies directly to pi* - the document names this as "the default whenever the same judge supplies both the stopping signal and the outcome" without noticing that T8 requires exactly that configuration.
minimal_repair: Split the claim by channel. State T8 in two versions: (a) programmatic outcome computable at decision time from H_t - stop arm known, no optimism, and require that psi be programmatic, not judge-based, for any horizon result (this is consistent with §12.7's "programmatic outcomes are ... a precondition for the horizon results"); (b) judge-based outcome with independent channels - stop arm is an estimated nuisance, T8's DP inherits P24(ii)'s optimism, and the learned pi*'s value must be re-estimated on a held-out scoring draw with the optimism bound reported. Delete the unqualified "known stop-arm value" from §0.2.5.

claim: T16: "Lambda is a function of (A-tilde_t, H_t) only (A12), so capping it per generator or including binned Lambda as a design coordinate involves no post-treatment conditioning, and contrasts of severity/specificity within a Lambda bin are identified by T3"; operationally "bin it; stratify randomization on the bin"; §13(c) "Leakage is a pre-treatment design coordinate, not a mediator."
why_wrong: A-tilde_t is the treatment. A function of the realized treatment is post-treatment by definition; calling it "pre-treatment" because it is computable from (A-tilde_t, H_t) is a category error - by that criterion the treatment itself is pre-treatment. Two separate defects follow. (i) Analysis-stage stratification on realized Lambda is post-treatment conditioning on a collider-adjacent variable: generators differ in their Lambda distributions, so within a bin the generator label becomes dependent on the residual decoding noise and on unbinned content quality, and the within-bin generator contrast is not the T3 contrast. (ii) "Stratify randomization on the bin" is not implementable in the stated order, because Lambda is unknown until A-tilde_t is drawn. The only implementable version is a *redefined action space*: generator k restricted to {Lambda in b}, i.e. the kernel q_k(· | h, Lambda in b). That is legitimate and T3 applies to it, but (a) its propensity acquires the normalizer P_{q_k}(Lambda in b | h), which is not exactly known (the document's own D2 catalogue lists rejection sampling as breaking exact propensity computability), and (b) it carries a new, quietly assumed positivity condition P_{q_k}(Lambda in b | h) > 0 for every k and every bin b compared, at every history - which will fail exactly where it matters, since a maximally severe/specific generator may never emit a low-leakage message.
minimal_repair: Rewrite T16 in terms of the restricted kernels: define the treatment as (generator k, leakage bin b), state the positivity requirement P_{q_k}(Lambda in b | h) >= delta_Lambda as a new assumption with a measured diagnostic (per-generator per-bin acceptance rates at every history stratum), and note that the restricted kernel's propensity is Monte-Carlo estimated rather than exactly known, so T9's exact unbiasedness degrades to the estimated-e case with A18's cross-term rate. Delete "no post-treatment conditioning" and §13(c)'s "pre-treatment design coordinate", replacing them with "leakage is a coordinate of a refined action space, not a covariate".

claim: P4: "rho^mar_t = [sum_k pi_t(k|H_t) q_k(A-tilde_t|H_t)] / [sum_k e_t(k|H_t) q_k(A-tilde_t|H_t)] = E[rho^sel_t | H_t, A-tilde_t], so it is valid, has weakly smaller variance by conditional Jensen ... Rule: marginalize over every recorded latent randomization whose density you can compute." Against T9(iii) "because K is finite, V-hat_t(h) = sum_k pi_t(k|h) Q-hat_t(h,k) is an exact finite sum - no summation over text".
location: P4 (§3); T9(iii) (§5); §0.1 "STOP is one of the selectors"
why_wrong: Two defects. (i) The displayed sums run over all k in K, including STOP, for which there is no emitted message and no density q_STOP(a-tilde | h) on L - so rho^mar is undefined at any stop turn, and the "marginalize out K" argument fails structurally because the stopping event is K-measurable and therefore cannot be integrated out of the trajectory. (ii) P4 and T9(iii) are incompatible as an estimator. rho^mar_t is sigma(H_t, A-tilde_t)-measurable while Q-hat_t(H_t, K_t) is K-measurable, so E[rho^mar_t Q-hat_t(H_t,K_t) | H_t] != sum_k pi_t(k|h) Q-hat_t(h,k); the telescoping identity that delivers T9(i)'s exact unbiasedness breaks, and restoring it requires the matched nuisance E[V_{t+1} | H_t, A-tilde_t] with V-hat_t(h) = sum over A-tilde of the marginal target kernel - i.e. exactly the summation over text that T9(iii) advertises as avoided. So the variance reduction of P4 and the finite-sum, text-critic-free DR of T9(iii) cannot both be had.
minimal_repair: State rho^mar only on continuation turns, with the stop coordinate carried as a separate exact factor: w_t = pi(STOP|h)/e(STOP|h) on stop turns, and [(1-pi(STOP))/(1-e(STOP))] x [sum_{k != STOP} pi q_k / sum_{k != STOP} e q_k] on continuation turns; re-derive the Jensen and 1/delta claims for that form. Then restrict P4 to the IPW and clipped-IPW estimators (E4, and the T20 certificate, where it is a pure variance win), and state explicitly that the sequential-DR estimator E1 must use the selector-level weight to retain exact unbiasedness - or accept a text-conditioned critic.

claim: T25(d): "Separable effects with isolation enforceable by interface construction ... an arm that shows a persistence-relevant signal to the user and provably withholds it from the model's context is verifiable by inspecting the rendered prompt - a software guarantee, not a statistical test. In medicine the decomposition is hypothetical; here it is code." Echoed in §13(c).
why_wrong: Code enforces only the trivial half of the isolation conditions. Withholding A_D from the receiver's context guarantees that A_D does not enter M directly. The non-trivial dismissibility condition - that A_D affects Y only through the continuation event, and that A_Y affects the continuation decision only through O_t - is a claim about the *user's* behavioural kernel, and it is false in the obvious implementation: a displayed cost meter, confidence indicator or progress bar plausibly changes what the user writes conditional on continuing, hence H_{t+1}, hence Y. With a simulated user, A_D is inserted into the simulated user's prompt, and an LLM conditioning on its whole context will in general alter both its stop head and its message content, so "reaching only the user's continuation decision" is architecturally false unless the simulated user is split into two calls with disjoint contexts - at which point the estimand is relative to that artificial split rather than to "the user".
minimal_repair: Restate: interface construction discharges the *receiver-side* isolation condition by construction and reduces the remaining assumption to a single behavioural condition on the user kernel (A_D affects the message distribution given continuation not at all). Label that condition as assumed, give it a number, and give the falsification test that is actually available: in the harness, branch on A_D at fixed A_Y and test whether the conditional distribution of the next message given continuation is invariant. Delete "in medicine hypothetical, here code" or restrict it to the receiver-side half.

claim: P22: after correctly withdrawing the unrestricted claim with the e_1 = 0.01 counterexample, the section's reporting device reads "at most X points of quality are recoverable by any implementable stopping rule; our learned rule recovers Y of them, with the upper bound resting on essentially no assumptions". Also "Prophet inequalities bound how much of the gap an online rule can capture (the i.i.d. constant ≈ 0.745)."
location: P22 (§7), the sandwich display and the following two paragraphs
why_wrong: Three defects. (i) The reporting device recommits the error the same proposition just corrected: the sandwich holds only for the *truncated* rule tau' = min(tau,T), i.e. only for rules that can shorten the natural conversation and never extend it. Regimes that force continuation past the natural stop - the whole point of P23 and of §0.4's Ext-E - can exceed E[max_{t<=T} psi(H_t)], by the document's own counterexample. "Any implementable stopping rule" is therefore false as written. (ii) "Essentially no assumptions" / "identified by consistency alone" understates: equating the observed psi(H_{tau'}) with the value of the truncated regime requires A21 (no decay, artifact-valued outcome) and the T8 structure that stopping at t yields exactly psi(H_t) - otherwise stopping early changes the measured outcome. (iii) The 0.745 constant is the i.i.d. prophet-inequality constant for independent draws from a known distribution. psi(H_1),...,psi(H_T) is a dependent, non-stationary adapted process with a random endogenous horizon; no constant-factor prophet guarantee holds for dependent sequences (even the independent non-identical case gives only 1/2). Quoting 0.745 here is not a conservative approximation, it is inapplicable.
minimal_repair: Change the reporting device to "at most X points of quality are recoverable by any rule that only shortens the natural conversation", and add one sentence saying that continuation-extending regimes are not bounded by this benchmark and require P23's weights. Add "under A21 and the known-stop-arm structure" to the identification claim. Delete the 0.745 figure, or replace it with an explicitly simulator-computed competitive ratio for the actual (dependent) psi process.

claim: T28 term 1: "a coarsened per-turn discrepancy ||S_# U_t(·|h) - S_# U-hat_t(·|h)||_1 scaled by (1/2) span(q-bar_t(h,·)) - the real-user factor IS estimable from ordinary unbranched logs with a classifier for S"; and "a coarsening residual rho_t = E|Q_t - q-bar_t|" as a single term.
why_wrong: (i) The term is a per-history L1 distance between two conditional action laws at H_t ~ P^U. Real-user logs contain each text history exactly once, so ||S_# U_t(·|h) - S_# U-hat_t(·|h)||_1 is not estimable at h; it is estimable only after pooling across histories via a smoothed model of U_t(·|h), which is precisely the extrapolation over long never-repeating text states that §5 and §15.2 correctly declare unverifiable. So term 1 is not "estimable from ordinary unbranched logs" - it is estimable only under an unverified smoothness assumption, which puts it in the same epistemic class as the transport term the document does flag. (ii) The residual bound produces two residual terms, not one: |int (U - U-hat) Q| <= |int (U - U-hat) q-bar∘S| + int U|Q - q-bar| + int U-hat|Q - q-bar|, i.e. rho^U_t (real-user action law, only partially replayable) plus rho^{U-hat}_t (simulator law, branchable). Collapsing them into one rho_t hides that one of the two is the harder object. (iii) Presentationally, the displayed identity is exact with H_t ~ P^U and therefore has no third term; the "three named terms" arise only after replacing P^U by P^{U-hat}. As written the identity and the bound are conflated.
minimal_repair: Relabel term 1 as "estimable only under a stated smoothness/pooling model for U_t(·|h)", and give the model and its diagnostic, or demote it alongside the transport term. Split rho_t into rho^U_t and rho^{U-hat}_t with their separate estimability statuses. Display the exact identity and the bound as two separate equations so the history-shift term's origin (the change of measure from P^U to P^{U-hat}) is visible.

claim: P21: "Late-continuation regimes are therefore not point-identified from logs; the sharp identified set has width kappa_0(pi) = P^pi(exists t < tau: e_t(CONT|H_t) = 0), sharpened to one-sided under free disposal." With §0.4's "Ext-E ... the strongest possible identification position ... Leakage-immune by construction" and D3 row (i) "stop-coordinate blips ... under exchangeability for the binary coordinate only".
location: P21 (§7); §0.4 table, Ext-E row; §10 ladder, D3 bullet (i)
why_wrong: The width kappa_0 is the sharp set width *conditional on A7 holding for the continuation coordinate*. But the mechanism P21 invokes to motivate the positivity failure - "the natural continuation probability decreases in current quality: satisfied users stop" - is simultaneously an exchangeability violation whenever the user's perceived quality exceeds what H_t records (and the document elsewhere insists the recorded signal S_t is a noisy judge channel, not the user's private assessment). So on the supported histories the estimator is not consistent for the regime value either, and the true identified set is strictly wider than kappa_0 in a way no computation of kappa_0 will reveal. §10 itself lists A7 for D3 as "assumed, untestable", and §15.8 lists calibration for exactly this as OPEN - which is inconsistent with P21 asserting sharpness and with §0.4 calling Ext-E "the strongest possible identification position". Separately, kappa_0 is stated as the width of the set for V(pi) = E[Y^pi]; for the cost-priced value E[Y^pi - lambda C^pi] the unsupported event carries unbounded extra cost, so the width is not kappa_0.
minimal_repair: State P21 as: "under A7 for the continuation coordinate, the sharp set has width kappa_0"; add that the same behavioural mechanism that creates the support failure also threatens A7, so kappa_0 is a lower bound on the true ambiguity, and point to §15.8. In §0.4 replace "the strongest possible identification position" with "the weakest positivity requirement", since the exchangeability burden is unchanged. Restate the width for the cost-priced objective as kappa_0 * range(Y - lambda C) with C bounded by the cap.

claim: T20: "With Y - lambda C in [0,1] and V-hat_M(pi) = ...", (a) "Clipping bias is sign-definite: 0 <= V(pi) - E[V-hat_M]", and T8: "a budget-constrained optimum equals the unpenalized optimum of E[Y^pi - lambda C^pi] for some lambda >= 0 by LP duality ... lambda is a budget price, not a hyperparameter". Plus E5/T13 feeding Y-tilde in [-1,1] into the same machinery.
why_wrong: (i) The dual price lambda is determined by the *estimated* attainable (value, cost) frontier. A finite-sample, one-sided certificate computed at a data-chosen lambda is not valid at the stated level: the event being covered was selected using the same data. "Not a hyperparameter" is true economically and false statistically. (ii) T20(a)'s sign-definiteness and the bound E[min(W,M)^2] <= M E[W] = M both require a non-negative outcome. The prioritized pseudo-outcome Y-tilde in [-1,1] (T13, E5) violates this, so for the prioritized objective clipping bias is not sign-definite and the certificate is not conservative in the direction claimed. (iii) With the recommended M = delta^{-d} there is in fact no clipping at all, so bias is zero and the E[W^2]/M bound is vacuous; that is benign but should be said, because it is the only reason (a) is not load-bearing in the primary route.
minimal_repair: Require lambda to be pre-registered (from a pilot budget, before outcomes are examined) whenever the certificate is reported, and state that the LP-duality reading of lambda is a post-hoc interpretation, not a licence to select lambda on the analysis sample. For the prioritized objective, certify on (Y-tilde + 1)/2 in [0,1] and restate T20(a),(b),(d) in those units. Add one line noting that M = delta^{-d} implies zero clipping bias, so (a) matters only when M < delta^{-d}.

claim: E2: "g-estimation of a choke-point SNMM for blips. sum_i sum_t d(H_it){1{K_it = k} - e_t(k|H_it)} U_it(beta) = 0 with U_it(beta) = Y_i - sum_{s >= t} gamma_s(H_is, K_is; beta)"; and §1's blip definition gamma_t(H_t, k, k_ref) = E[Y^{(k at t, then ref)} - Y^{(k_ref at t, then ref)} | H_t].
why_wrong: STOP is one of the treatment levels, so the treatment at turn t changes the *number of subsequent turns*. Then (a) the contrast gamma_t(H_t, STOP, k_ref) has "then ref" vacuous on one arm and non-vacuous on the other, so the two arms of the blip have different horizon supports, and (b) the additive representation U_it = Y_i - sum_{s >= t} gamma_s has an index set {t,...,T_i} whose upper limit is itself a function of the treatments being blipped down. The blip-down identity E[U_it | H_it] = E[Y^{(ref from t)} | H_it] therefore does not follow from the displayed definitions: it requires the reference regime to be defined on all histories up to the administrative cap and each gamma_s to be defined as "realized action versus reference, holding all later actions at the reference", with gamma at a STOP turn absorbing the entire value of the turns that never occurred. None of that is stated, and A14 ("singleton or pinned reference arm") does not supply it.
minimal_repair: Fix the reference as a continuation regime defined to turn K-bar (never STOP), state the blip-down convention explicitly - gamma_s(H_s, STOP) := E[Y^{(ref from s)} | H_s] - psi(H_s), i.e. the full remaining-turn effect - and rewrite U_it with the index set {t,...,min(T_i, K-bar)} and an explicit STOP term. Then re-check that the estimating equation's conditional mean-zero property still holds turn by turn.

claim: T9(i): "With e known, E[psi-hat] = psi for any Q-hat whatsoever", repeated in §0.2.3 as "sequential DR is exactly unbiased for any outcome model whatsoever (T9) ... a cheap badly-calibrated LLM critic carries zero bias risk". Primary estimator E1 is "Cross-fitted one-step / TMLE with known weights".
why_wrong: Exact unbiasedness requires two conditions that are not stated in T9(i) and one of which the recommended estimator violates. (a) Q-hat must be independent of the evaluation sample - without cross-fitting, E[psi-hat] != psi, and "for any Q-hat whatsoever" as written covers same-sample fits. (b) The telescoping needs internal consistency V-hat_t(h) = sum_k pi_t(k|h) Q-hat_t(h,k); a critic that emits V-hat directly, or independently fitted V-hat and Q-hat, destroys it (and P10's branch-augmented version survives only because the two rollout estimates agree *in expectation*, which is worth saying). (c) The TMLE variant fluctuates Q-hat using the same data through the clever-covariate score, so its fitted values are data-dependent and finite-sample exactness does not hold - only asymptotic validity does. So the flagship robustness claim does not apply to the flagship estimator.
minimal_repair: Restate T9(i) as: "for any Q-hat that is fixed conditional on the evaluation fold and satisfies V-hat_t = sum_k pi_t Q-hat_t, E[psi-hat] = psi exactly." Add that the cross-fitted one-step estimator attains this and the TMLE variant does not (it is asymptotically equivalent but not finite-sample exact), and amend §0.2.3's "zero bias risk" to "zero asymptotic bias and, for the cross-fitted one-step form, exact finite-sample unbiasedness".

claim: P18(a): "E[W_{1:t} g(H_t)] = E^pi[g(H_t)] for every t gives a family of specification checks ... A run that does not report (a)-(d) is not an experiment."
why_wrong: Under an endogenous horizon, W_{1:t} and H_t are undefined on {T < t}, and E^pi[g(H_t)] presupposes reaching t under pi. The correct identity is E[W_{1:t} 1{T >= t} g(H_t)] = E^pi[1{T^pi >= t} g(H_t)], or the stopped version with t ∧ T. The naive form will report violations on any trajectory set with early stopping, i.e. it will flag false positives exactly in the regime the paper cares about - and this is offered as a mandatory diagnostic.
minimal_repair: Replace with the stopped/indicator form and say which of the two (restricted-to-reached or stopped-process) is being computed; note that the right-hand side must be computed from the same indicator so the check is an equality of two identified quantities.

claim: P12: "Because c(v,w) = 1{v > w} is neither supermodular nor submodular, the extrema are not attained at the comonotone/antimonotone couplings, so no Fréchet-Hoeffding closed form is available in general (the draft's scalar reduction is withdrawn)" and "the sharp identified set is the value range of an optimal-transport LP".
location: P12 (§7); §13(a) bibliography line citing Makarov 1981, Rüschendorf 1982
why_wrong: The premise is correct (I verified both directions fail: v=1, v'=3, w=0, w'=2 breaks submodularity; v=0, v'=1, w=0, w'=1 breaks supermodularity), and so is the conclusion that the extrema are not at the comonotone/antimonotone couplings. But the further conclusion is too strong: sharp bounds on P(V > W) = 1 - P(V - W <= 0) under fixed marginals are exactly the Makarov/Rüschendorf bounds on the distribution of a difference, which have closed form as an inf/sup over a threshold of the marginal CDFs - and those references are already in the document's own bibliography. An LP is not needed for the two-level case; it is needed for the three-level lexicographic case, which §15.6 correctly lists as open.
minimal_repair: Change to: "the extrema are not attained at the comonotone/antimonotone couplings, so the naive Fréchet-Hoeffding substitution fails; the sharp bounds are nonetheless closed-form via Makarov-Rüschendorf for a scalar comparison, and require an optimal-transport LP only for the multi-level lexicographic comparison (§15.6)."

claim: T7 design corollary: "Micro-randomizing one uniformly chosen turn per trajectory therefore identifies the turn-s blip with effective sample size of order n*delta/T (the 1/T is the turn-selection factor and must not be dropped)." And P10: "Since alpha_t grows in t: spend the branching budget late, where the weights have already degenerated."
why_wrong: Both omit the reach probability under an endogenous horizon. A trajectory randomized at turn s contributes only if it reaches s, so the ESS is of order n*delta*P(T >= s)/T, not n*delta/T - and the document's own P21 says late histories are rare because satisfied users stop, so the omitted factor is smallest exactly at the turns of interest. The same omission drives P10's allocation rule: the variance expression has no P(T >= t) and no roll-in cost (P5b has c_0, P10 does not), so the conclusion "spend the branching budget late" is derived from a budget constraint sum_t c_t m_t <= B that does not charge for reaching turn t. With a realistic reach profile the optimum can move earlier.
minimal_repair: Insert P(T >= s) into the T7 ESS statement. In P10, write the variance as sum_t P(T >= t)[E[W^2_{1:t}] sigma^2_{Q,t}/m_t + ...] and the budget as sum_t (c_0 t + c_t) m_t P(T >= t) <= B, then restate the allocation and say that "spend late" holds only when the growth in E[W^2_{1:t}] outruns the decay in P(T >= t) - a measurable condition, not a theorem.

claim: P5: "E[W^2_{1:T}] = E[Gamma_1], Gamma_{T+1} ≡ 1, Gamma_t(h) = E[w_t^2 Gamma_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) | H_t = h]" and "E[W^2_{1:T}] = E_{P-tilde}[prod_{t=1}^T (1 + chi_t^2(H_t))], pi-tilde_t(k|h) ∝ pi_t(k|h)^2/e_t(k|h)".
why_wrong: The algebra is correct (I verified the squared-kernel measure change and the failure of the naive product identity), but T is a random, action-determined horizon and the two displays use it under different laws: in the first, T is the P-horizon and the recursion needs the convention Gamma_{t+1} := 1 on {K_t = STOP}; in the second, the product runs to the P-tilde-horizon, since the tilted kernel pi-tilde ∝ pi^2/e also re-weights the STOP selector and therefore changes the stopping law. Left as written, the identity reads as if the same T appears on both sides.
minimal_repair: State the STOP convention for Gamma explicitly, and write the second display as E_{P-tilde}[prod_{t=1}^{T-tilde}(1 + chi_t^2(H_t))] with T-tilde the horizon under P-tilde, noting that P-tilde also tilts the stopping probability.

claim: T27: "R-hat = n^{-1} sum_i (gamma-hat - gamma-tilde)^2 - n^{-1} sum_i v-hat is unbiased for the true conditional-effect risk ... v(h) needs n_b >= 2 per arm - hence the deep benchmark slice of P5b." With P5b: wide training slice at n_b = 1, narrow deep benchmark slice.
why_wrong: Unbiasedness of R-hat requires E[v-hat] = E_{val}[v], i.e. the variance offset must be an average over the *same* history distribution as the squared-error term. P5b places v-estimation in a narrow deep slice (n_b >= 8) and the wide slice at n_b = 1, where v cannot be estimated at all. Importing the deep slice's average v is valid only if the two slices share the history law; since the deep slice is deliberately narrow and selected, that is exactly what will fail. The document flags the continuation-regime mismatch and the branch-history restriction but not this one.
minimal_repair: Either estimate v on a random subsample of the *validation* histories (n_b = 2 suffices for unbiasedness even with high variance), or state the requirement that the deep slice be a uniform random subsample of the wide slice's histories and verify it. Alternatively lean on the ranking use, where the offset cancels and no v estimate is needed - and say that the absolute risk number requires the matched-slice condition.

claim: T26(a): branch data identify Q_t, blips, V(pi) "with no ignorability and no positivity assumption over L, because we never form density ratios"; §0.3: "without structure, optimizing over history-dependent regimes needs Omega(K^T) rollouts (T26), which is the formal reason a learned blip estimator is mandatory".
why_wrong: (i) "No positivity assumption" is contradicted two lines later by T26(b): a regime selecting an unexpanded action at a positively-reached node is not identified. That *is* the positivity condition, relocated from L to the expanded tree. (ii) §0.3 conflates identification with query complexity. T26(c) is a lower bound on the number of leaf queries needed to *find* the optimum under a needle construction; it says nothing about whether V(pi) is identified, which T26(a) grants for every executable pi. And a learned blip estimator does not evade the lower bound - it evades it only by importing structure, which in the region where the structure extrapolates is an identifying assumption (as T7 itself says).
minimal_repair: Rewrite T26(a) as "positivity holds by construction on the expanded action set at every design-reached node, and fails precisely off-tree (T26(b))". In §0.3 say "needs Omega(K^T) rollouts to *search*" and add that a learned blip model substitutes an extrapolation assumption for the query budget, cross-referencing T7's labelling requirement.

claim: §1, closing sentence of the confounding discussion: "Adjustment recovers the truth - and adjustment is only available once the treatment has been coarsened, because at the fine level there is no cell to adjust within."
why_wrong: Misdiagnosis. The adjustment set is the history stratum (good/bad in the worked example), and history strata exist regardless of how finely the treatment is defined - coarsening the treatment does not create cells to adjust within, it creates cells with positive treatment probability. The correct statement is that standardization needs positivity of the treatment *within* history strata, which fails at the fine level. As written it suggests the confounder discretization is what coarsening buys.
minimal_repair: Replace with "...because at the fine level no treatment level has positive probability within a history stratum, so the standardized mean is not estimable." (The numerical example itself checks exactly: +0.125 average benefit, -0.13 marginal comparison.)

claim: T30 / §13(b) contribution 3: "the action-level text critic disappears" and "exact two-sided double robustness"; against T30's own concession that "the soft-optimal recursion still needs a text-conditioned critic at history-action pairs never observed".
why_wrong: The EIF's residual term involves Q-tilde_{t+1}(H_{t+1}), and H_{t+1} = (H_t, A-tilde_t, O_t, ...) contains the realized message - so the critic is action-dependent. What actually disappears is the need to *integrate* the critic over L (it is evaluated only at the observed action). "The action-level text critic disappears" therefore overstates a real and clean result, and is contradicted within the same subsection.
minimal_repair: Restate as "no integration of the critic over the action space is required: the critic is evaluated only at observed history-action pairs", and keep the existing concession about the soft-optimal recursion as the limit of that claim.
